question: A nurse is preparing to apply a prescribed topical corticosteroid to an infected, weeping skin ulcer. What initial action is most critical?

options.A: Assessing the skin condition and checking the specific order against the patient chart
options.B: Applying an airtight plastic wrap over the ulcer immediately
options.C: Scrubbing the ulcer vigorously with an antiseptic brush
options.D: Warming the ointment tube under direct sunlight

explanation: Safety requires verifying the medication order and evaluating the skin status to ensure the treatment is safe for the current tissue condition. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h4)

question: In which direction should a nurse smooth a topical cream onto a patient's hairy forearm?

options.A: Against the direction of hair growth
options.B: In the direction of hair growth
options.C: In a vigorous circular scrubbing motion
options.D: Vertically from wrist to elbow only

explanation: Smoothing medication in the direction of hair growth prevents irritation and inflammation of the hair follicles, known as folliculitis. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h5)

question: A student nurse is about to scoop an ointment from a multi-dose jar for a patient. What action demonstrates correct technique?

options.A: Using a clean wooden spatula or tongue depressor to remove the ointment
options.B: Pouring sterile water directly into the jar to liquefy the contents
options.C: Using a gloved bare finger to scoop out the required amount
options.D: Warming the entire multi-use container in a microwave before use

explanation: Using a clean spatula prevents microbial contamination of the remaining medication inside a multi-dose container. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h5)

question: Which of the following is a common local complication associated with the prolonged misuse of potent topical corticosteroids?

options.A: Skin atrophy and thinning
options.B: Permanent systemic hypertension
options.C: Hypertrophic hair growth
options.D: Gastrointestinal ulceration

explanation: Prolonged use of potent topical steroids breaks down collagen and dermal matrix proteins, leading to visible skin thinning and atrophy. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h6)

question: Why must a nurse wear gloves when applying potent hormonal or nitroglycerin ointments to a patient?

options.A: To prevent the nurse from accidentally absorbing the potent medication through their own skin
options.B: To keep the patient's skin sterile during the application process
options.C: To warm the medication faster before it touches the patient
options.D: To prevent the medication from staining the patient's bed linens

explanation: Potent drugs can easily cross the skin barrier of healthcare workers during application, leading to occupational exposure and unwanted systemic effects. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h6)

question: What key instruction should a nurse give a patient regarding the thickness of topical cream application?

options.A: Mix the cream with petroleum jelly to double the batch size
options.B: Apply a thick, heavy layer so the skin stays moist all day
options.C: Massage the cream aggressively until it completely disappears into the fat layer
options.D: Apply only a thin, even layer as prescribed, because excess does not speed healing

explanation: Skin can only absorb a specific amount of medication at a time; applying excess cream wastes product and increases systemic absorption risks. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h7)

question: A patient is discharged home with a prescription for a potent medicated skin ointment. Which statement by the patient indicates a need for FURTHER teaching?

options.A: I will call the clinic if I develop a severe burning rash where the cream was put.
options.B: I will wrap the treated area tightly in polythene nylon to make it heal twice as fast.
options.C: I will rotate the placement site for my transdermal patches every single time.
options.D: I will wash my hands thoroughly after applying my ointment every time.

explanation: Occlusive wrapping increases systemic absorption and toxicity risks unless specifically ordered by a doctor, making this statement incorrect. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary objective of medical asepsis?

options.A: Destroying viruses through chemical immersion
options.B: Sterilizing all surgical instrumentation
options.C: Reducing the total number of microorganisms
options.D: Eliminating every single bacterial spore

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on lowering microbial loads to prevent transmission, unlike surgical asepsis which aims for complete elimination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: How should a nurse handle an object when its sterile status is uncertain?

options.A: Use the object only for minor dressing changes
options.B: Inspect the packaging for minor dust particles
options.C: Rinse the item with sterile water before use
options.D: Assume the object is contaminated

explanation: A core principle of aseptic technique dictates that any doubt regarding sterility requires immediate rejection of the item. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h1)

question: Which clinical procedure requires the strict application of surgical asepsis?

options.A: Performing a routine bed bath for an adult
options.B: Feeding a patient via a nasogastric tube
options.C: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
options.D: Administering an oral antibiotic suspension

explanation: Catheterization introduces a conduit directly into the sterile urinary bladder, demanding a completely sterile approach. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: What is the fundamental difference between clean technique and sterile technique?

options.A: Clean technique requires sterile gloves while sterile technique uses examination gloves
options.B: Clean technique reduces microbial load while sterile technique eliminates all microorganisms
options.C: Clean technique is performed only by doctors while sterile technique belongs to nurses
options.D: Clean technique applies to surgery while sterile technique applies to outpatient wards

explanation: Medical asepsis decreases the number of pathogens, whereas surgical asepsis achieves total microbial eradication. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h2)

question: Which link in the chain of infection is directly interrupted by performing hand hygiene?

options.A: Infectious agent
options.B: Mode of transmission
options.C: Reservoir source
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: Washing hands removes transient microorganisms, preventing them from traveling between patients or surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: A contaminated dressing tray acting as a breeding ground for bacteria represents which element of the infection chain?

options.A: Portal of entry
options.B: Infectious exit
options.C: Susceptible host
options.D: Reservoir

explanation: A reservoir is any environment where a pathogen can live, grow, and multiply before infecting a host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h3)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly preferred over alcohol-based rubs?

options.A: When hands are visibly soiled with organic material
options.B: Before entering a general medical outpatient ward
options.C: Immediately after checking a patient's blood pressure
options.D: When touching unsoiled patient chart folders

explanation: Visible dirt and certain spore-forming pathogens require physical friction and washing with soap and water to clear effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: A nurse finishes taking vital signs for a patient with intact skin and no visible body fluids. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Put on sterile gloves before touching the next chart
options.B: Rinse hands under cold running water without soap
options.C: Wash hands rigorously with medicated bar soap
options.D: Perform hand hygiene using an alcohol-based rub

explanation: For routine non-soiled patient contact, alcohol-based hand rubs provide rapid and efficient microbial reduction. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h4)

question: Which item of personal protective equipment must be removed first when undressing after a procedure?

options.A: Goggles
options.B: Mask
options.C: Gloves
options.D: Gown

explanation: Gloves carry the highest concentration of contaminants and are removed first to prevent transferring pathogens to other surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the primary reason for wearing an N95 respirator instead of a standard surgical mask?

options.A: Providing sterile protection during major abdominal surgery
options.B: Filtering tiny airborne droplet nuclei circulating in the air
options.C: Preventing large fluid splashes from arterial blood spurts
options.D: Shielding the wearer from direct contact with intact skin

explanation: Respirators create a tight seal capable of filtering out microscopic airborne pathogens like tuberculosis bacilli. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h5)

question: What width defines the unsterile border around the outer edge of a sterile drape?

options.A: One inch
options.B: Six centimeters
options.C: Three inches
options.D: Half a meter

explanation: Standard protocol dictates that the outer one-inch margin of any sterile field is unsterile due to handling during setup. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: Why must a nurse never turn their back on an established sterile field?

options.A: Sterile forceps will automatically slide off the edge of the metal table
options.B: Unobserved areas can become accidentally contaminated without the nurse knowing
options.C: Air currents from the back will blow dust particles onto the sterile supplies
options.D: Hospital regulations require continuous visual supervision of all trays

explanation: Maintaining visual contact ensures that any accidental breach of sterility is immediately noticed and corrected. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h6)

question: How should a nurse manage hand hygiene during unexpected water shortages in a clinic?

options.A: Postpone all direct patient care until municipal water supply returns
options.B: Wear examination gloves continuously without changing between tasks
options.C: Wipe hands clean with standard paper towels without applying liquids
options.D: Use stored water systems like tippy-taps or alcohol-based hand rubs

explanation: Alternative water delivery setups and alcohol rubs maintain infection control standards during municipal supply disruptions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a direct consequence of healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Increased financial burden on families
options.B: Decreased overall length of hospital stay
options.C: Prolonged recovery periods for patients
options.D: Elevated risk of patient mortality

explanation: HAIs invariably prolong hospital stays rather than shortening them, making infection prevention vital. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T1#GNS122_U2_T1_h7)

question: What is the primary objective of medical asepsis in clinical practice?

options.A: Reducing the number and spread of microorganisms
options.B: Preventing airborne transmission of viral spores
options.C: Sterilizing surgical instruments prior to use
options.D: Eliminating all microbial life from an object

explanation: Medical asepsis focuses on decreasing pathogen load and limiting transmission, unlike surgical asepsis which seeks complete sterility. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Why must hand hygiene still be performed immediately before donning medical gloves?

options.A: Soap permanently alters the pH of the epidermal outer layer
options.B: Moist skin inside gloves accelerates rapid microbial proliferation
options.C: Glove manufacturing leaves toxic chemical residues on surfaces
options.D: Synthetic polymers chemically react with residual body oils

explanation: The warm, enclosed space inside a glove creates an ideal breeding ground for bacteria already present on the skin if hands are unwashed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which clinical scenario strictly requires the use of clean medical gloves?

options.A: Assisting an ambulatory patient to walk down the hallway
options.B: Measuring a patient's blood pressure over an intact shirt sleeve
options.C: Feeding an independent adult patient a standard hospital meal
options.D: Emptying a urinary drainage collection bag in the ward

explanation: Urine is a bodily fluid with high potential for contamination, requiring barrier protection during disposal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What dual purpose do medical gloves serve in the hospital environment?

options.A: Enhancing manual grip strength when handling wet clinical equipment
options.B: Providing complete hand sterilization during prolonged surgical procedures
options.C: Protecting staff from infection and preventing pathogen transfer to patients
options.D: Replacing the need for routine hand washing between patient rooms

explanation: Gloves act as a two-way shield, safeguarding both the healthcare worker and the patient from cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h2)

question: What is a key physical design difference between examination and surgical gloves?

options.A: Surgical gloves are packaged in non-sterile bulk cardboard dispensers
options.B: Examination gloves feature exact sizing numbers for each finger length
options.C: Surgical gloves are manufactured with specific left and right hand shapes
options.D: Examination gloves include extended cuffs to cover surgical gowns

explanation: Surgical gloves are anatomically shaped for left and right hands to reduce fatigue and improve dexterity during long procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: When is it appropriate to utilize non-sterile examination gloves in patient care?

options.A: During an open reduction and internal fixation of a fractured femur
options.B: While inserting a central venous catheter into the subclavian vein
options.C: When performing a routine venipuncture on intact skin
options.D: During the surgical repair of an open abdominal hernia

explanation: Routine tasks like venipuncture involve contact with blood but do not breach sterile body cavities, making clean examination gloves sufficient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h3)

question: Which glove material provides the greatest resistance to punctures and chemical exposure?

options.A: Vinyl
options.B: Nitrile
options.C: Cellulose
options.D: Latex

explanation: Nitrile synthetic rubber offers superior puncture resistance and durability against harsh chemical agents compared to vinyl or latex. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: A staff member develops contact urticaria and respiratory symptoms when handling certain medical supplies. Which glove material is the most likely cause of this reaction?

options.A: Latex
options.B: Neoprene
options.C: Vinyl
options.D: Nitrile

explanation: Natural rubber latex contains proteins that frequently induce Type I immediate hypersensitivity reactions, presenting as hives or respiratory distress. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h4)

question: What part of a sterile glove is touched first when donning them using the open method?

options.A: The inside of the cuff fold
options.B: The exterior palm surface
options.C: The fingertips of the glove
options.D: The outer edge of the wrapper

explanation: Touching only the inside of the cuff fold protects the exterior sterile surface of the glove from contamination by unwashed or unsterile hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: During sterile glove application, what is the proper technique for putting the second glove onto the non-dominant hand?

options.A: Use your teeth to adjust the wrist placement after both hands are inside
options.B: Slide the sterile gloved fingers underneath the outer cuff fold of the second glove
options.C: Ask an assistant to hold the open cuff while you insert your hand quickly
options.D: Grip the outside finger surface with your bare hand and pull firmly upward

explanation: Gloved-to-gloved contact using the cuff fold maintains sterility by ensuring skin never touches the outer surface of the second glove. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h5)

question: Where should used contaminated gloves be disposed of immediately after removal?

options.A: In the patient's bedside trash can
options.B: In your uniform pocket for later disposal
options.C: On top of the medication preparation cart
options.D: Inside a designated clinical waste bin

explanation: Contaminated barriers must go directly into biohazard or clinical waste receptacles to prevent accidental exposure in the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: What is the primary rationale for turning gloves inside out as they are removed?

options.A: To trap potential pathogens on the inner surface away from skin
options.B: To compact the volume of waste inside the disposal bin
options.C: To prevent the latex material from sticking to your fingers
options.D: To make it easier for housekeeping staff to sort hospital trash

explanation: Inverting the gloves encapsulates the contaminated exterior surfaces, preventing infectious material from contacting the nurse's skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h6)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT acceptable when managing disposable medical gloves?

options.A: Applying alcohol-based hand rub to soiled gloves for reuse
options.B: Performing hand hygiene immediately after removing soiled gloves
options.C: Selecting a nitrile glove size that fits the hand snugly
options.D: Changing gloves between different body sites on the same patient

explanation: Disposable gloves are single-use items; chemical disinfectants degrade their structural integrity and they cannot be safely reused. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: A nurse wearing gloves touches a patient's infected pressure ulcer and then immediately touches the computer keyboard at the nurses' station. What has occurred?

options.A: The creation of a fomite-mediated cross-contamination route
options.B: A protocol-compliant transmission prevention method
options.C: An effective sterilization of the computer equipment
options.D: A standard violation of surgical asepsis guidelines only

explanation: Wearing contaminated gloves outside the immediate care zone transfers pathogens to high-touch environmental surfaces, endangering others. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h7)

question: Under Standard Precautions, when must healthcare personnel wear gloves?

options.A: Whenever anticipated contact involves blood, body fluids, or non-intact skin
options.B: Throughout the entire duration of an eight-hour hospital shift
options.C: Only when caring for patients with a confirmed diagnosis of HIV
options.D: Exclusively during sterile surgical procedures performed in the theatre

explanation: Standard Precautions mandate barrier use for any potential exposure to blood, body fluids, secretions, excretions, and non-intact skin for all patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)

question: A patient is admitted to the ward with a confirmed multidrug-resistant organism spread via touch. Which transmission-based precaution category applies, requiring mandatory glove use upon room entry?

options.A: Airborne Precautions
options.B: Protective Environment
options.C: Droplet Precautions
options.D: Contact Precautions

explanation: Contact Precautions are designed to prevent the spread of infectious agents transmitted by direct or indirect contact with the patient or their environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T10#GNS122_U2_T10_h8)

question: What is the primary function of a wound dressing compared to a bandage?

options.A: A dressing makes direct contact with the wound bed to absorb exudate.
options.B: A bandage delivers topical antibiotics directly to the subcutaneous tissue.
options.C: A bandage acts as the primary sterile barrier against bacterial entry.
options.D: A dressing provides structural support to immobilize a fractured limb.

explanation: Dressings are applied directly to the wound surface to manage drainage and protect the site, while bandages secure those dressings. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is maintaining a moist environment considered a key principle of modern wound dressings?

options.A: It discourages bacterial colonization by lowering local tissue temperature.
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for systemic antibiotic therapy.
options.C: It accelerates epithelial cell migration and prevents scab formation.
options.D: It reduces local blood supply to minimize post-operative bleeding.

explanation: A moist wound bed allows new skin cells to glide more easily across the surface, speeding up tissue regeneration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h1)

question: The primary purpose of maintaining thermal insulation at a wound site is to:

options.A: Stimulate peripheral vasoconstriction to control bleeding.
options.B: Optimize local enzymatic activity required for cellular repair.
options.C: Increase systemic metabolic rate and fever response.
options.D: Induce local hypothermia to prevent bacterial replication.

explanation: Keeping the wound at body temperature ensures that cellular enzymes function at peak efficiency during the healing process. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h2)

question: A patient's peri-wound skin appears white, soggy, and fragile. What objective of wound dressing management has failed?

options.A: Effective management and absorption of wound exudate
options.B: Maintenance of adequate thermal insulation
options.C: Provision of a rigid structural barrier against trauma
options.D: Prevention of systemic allergic reactions to tape

explanation: Maceration occurs when excess fluid sits on the skin, indicating that the dressing failed to properly absorb or contain wound drainage. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h2)

question: A full-thickness skin wound is characterized by involvement of which tissue layers?

options.A: Stratum corneum and superficial fascia
options.B: Subcutaneous tissue, muscle, or bone
options.C: Hair follicles and sebaceous glands exclusively
options.D: Epidermis and upper dermis only

explanation: Full-thickness wounds extend beyond the dermis into deeper structures, requiring extensive tissue regeneration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h3)

question: How does a clean-contaminated surgical wound differ fundamentally from a clean wound?

options.A: It involves entering a GI, respiratory, or urinary tract under controlled conditions.
options.B: It is caused by high-velocity blunt trauma in an unsterile environment.
options.C: It has been open to the air for longer than twenty-four hours.
options.D: It shows overt clinical signs of purulent drainage before closure.

explanation: Clean-contaminated wounds carry a low baseline risk of infection because luminal contents are accessed deliberately during scheduled procedures. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which dressing material forms a hydrophilic gel when it interacts with exudate and is best suited for bleeding or heavily draining wounds?

options.A: Transparent film
options.B: Alginate dressing
options.C: Hydrocolloid wafer
options.D: Dry woven gauze

explanation: Alginates derived from seaweed react with serum sodium to create a gel matrix that handles high volumes of fluid. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: A patient has a shallow sacral pressure ulcer with minimal exudate that requires autolytic debridement. Which dressing option is most appropriate?

options.A: Non-absorbent plastic wrap
options.B: Dry multi-layered gauze
options.C: High-absorbency alginate
options.D: Hydrocolloid dressing

explanation: Hydrocolloids maintain a moist environment that traps endogenous enzymes, facilitating autolytic breakdown of dead tissue in low-exudate wounds. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why is it clinically recommended to administer analgesics roughly thirty minutes before performing a complex dressing change?

options.A: To reach peak drug concentration when manipulation of the wound bed is most painful.
options.B: To induce systemic vasodilation and accelerate local blood flow to the wound.
options.C: To lower the patient's baseline core body temperature during the procedure.
options.D: To prevent the patient from experiencing nausea caused by antiseptic vapors.

explanation: Timing analgesia with the pharmacokinetic profile of the drug ensures maximum pain relief during uncomfortable debridement and cleansing steps. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h5)

question: What does a black, leathery area of tissue observed within a wound bed indicate?

options.A: Necrotic eschar
options.B: Serous exudate pooling
options.C: Healthy granulation
options.D: Epithelial migration

explanation: Eschar is dead, devitalized tissue that must typically be removed before a wound can progress through normal healing phases. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h5)

question: What is the correct directional rule for cleaning a wound during a dressing change?

options.A: In random circular motions across both the wound and surrounding tape
options.B: From the outer perimeter inward toward the center of the wound bed
options.C: From the least contaminated area to the most contaminated area
options.D: From the inferior border upward toward the superior anatomical margin

explanation: Moving from clean to dirty prevents dragging external bacteria or heavy exudate into cleaner parts of the wound bed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h6)

question: Which action represents a direct breach of sterile technique while setting up a bedside dressing tray?

options.A: Pouring normal saline solution without splashing the inner basin rim
options.B: Opening the outer wrapper of a sterile package away from your body first
options.C: Donning sterile gloves using an open or closed glove technique
options.D: Reaching across the sterile field with an unsterile arm to adjust a light

explanation: Any unsterile object or body part crossing over a sterile field contaminates the entire sterile workspace below it. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h6)

question: In what direction should a clinician pull when removing an old adhesive dressing from a patient's limb?

options.A: In circular twists until the adhesive tape loses its tackiness
options.B: Rapidly against the direction of hair growth to break adhesion
options.C: Upward and away from the skin at a sharp ninety-degree angle
options.D: Parallel to the skin and in the direction of hair growth

explanation: Pulling parallel to the skin reduces epidermal stripping and minimizes mechanical pain for the patient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h7)

question: Why is it necessary to remove the initial pair of clean gloves and perform hand hygiene before putting on sterile gloves for wound cleansing?

options.A: To test the integrity of the second pair of sterile gloves prior to touching the patient
options.B: To comply with hospital administrative policies regarding total glove consumption limits
options.C: To prevent transferring contaminants from the old dirty dressing to the sterile setup
options.D: To allow the skin of the hands to dry completely before putting on powder-free gloves

explanation: Gloves used to touch used dressings are contaminated and must be discarded before handling sterile supplies. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h7)

question: Which set of parameters must always be included when charting a routine wound assessment?

options.A: Dimensions, drainage characteristics, tissue color, and peri-wound skin condition
options.B: Patient dietary intake, blood pressure, urine output, and mobility score
options.C: Cost of dressing supplies, brand name of tape, and nurse badge number
options.D: Room temperature, humidity level, and visitor presence during the procedure

explanation: A complete clinical description focuses on physical measurements, exudate quality, bed composition, and adjacent tissue health. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h8)

question: What visual indicator in a wound bed provides the strongest evidence of healthy tissue regeneration?

options.A: Bright pink or red, moist, and bumpy granulation tissue
options.B: Dry, hard, and leathery black eschar covering the surface
options.C: Pale, translucent, and boggy tissue prone to immediate tearing
options.D: Excessive pooling of thick, yellow, foul-smelling purulent exudate

explanation: Granulation tissue indicates active neoangiogenesis and collagen deposition, which are essential steps in filling a healing wound bed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h8)

question: A patient following an exploratory laparotomy suddenly reports a 'popping' sensation after coughing, and loops of bowel are visible protruding through the abdominal incision. What is the immediate nursing priority?

options.A: Administer a stat dose of oral analgesics and prepare the patient for immediate bedside suture removal.
options.B: Cover the exposed viscera with sterile saline-soaked dressings and notify the surgeon immediately.
options.C: Position the patient flat on their stomach to relieve gravity pressure on the lower abdominal wall.
options.D: Gently push the protruding bowel loops back into the peritoneal cavity and apply tight abdominal binders.

explanation: Evisceration is a surgical emergency requiring moist sterile protection of exposed organs and urgent surgical intervention; never attempt re-insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h9)

question: Which clinical finding is NOT typically associated with a localized wound infection?

options.A: Progressive, worsening localized pain and tenderness
options.B: Purulent, cloudy, or foul-smelling drainage exudate
options.C: Localized swelling, warmth, and spreading skin redness
options.D: Cool, pale, and pulseless surrounding tissue borders

explanation: Cool, pale, and pulseless tissue points toward arterial compromise or ischemia rather than typical inflammatory infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T11#GNS122_U2_T11_h9)

question: What is the primary clinical risk of leaving suture material in place longer than necessary?

options.A: Immediate spontaneous wound dehiscence
options.B: Accelerated deterioration of underlying fascia
options.C: Increased risk of localized infection
options.D: Permanent systemic immunosuppression

explanation: Sutures act as foreign bodies that can harbor bacteria over time, making prolonged retention a primary risk factor for wound tract infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why must sutures be removed before complete epithelialization around the thread occurs?

options.A: To prevent painful removal and scarring
options.B: To speed up the systemic inflammatory response
options.C: To prevent the sutures from dissolving prematurely
options.D: To allow the surgeon to re-suture the area

explanation: When epithelium grows around the suture material, pulling it out causes unnecessary trauma, pain, and worse cosmetic scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h1)

question: Facial sutures are typically removed after how many days?

options.A: 14 to 21 days
options.B: 7 to 10 days
options.C: 28 to 30 days
options.D: 3 to 5 days

explanation: The face has an abundant blood supply enabling rapid healing, and early removal prevents permanent cross-hatch scarring. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: A patient had a deep laceration repaired over the knee joint ten days ago. What is the most appropriate nursing action regarding suture removal?

options.A: Delay removal and consult the prescriber
options.B: Remove half the sutures and leave the rest for a week
options.C: Soak the knee in warm water and pull all sutures out
options.D: Remove the sutures immediately as ten days has passed

explanation: Joints experience high physical tension and slower healing, often requiring 10 to 14 days or longer before sutures can be safely removed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h2)

question: What finding contraindicates the immediate removal of sutures during pre-assessment?

options.A: A slight itching sensation reported by the patient
options.B: Mild bruising around the surgical site
options.C: Incomplete wound closure or gaping edges
options.D: Dry brown crusting along the incision line

explanation: If the wound edges have not fully healed and still gape, removing sutures will cause wound dehiscence. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: What is the correct action if a nurse discovers localized purulent drainage and wound separation during pre-assessment?

options.A: Remove all sutures to let the pus drain out freely
options.B: Apply adhesive strips directly over the pus
options.C: Leave the sutures in place and notify the prescriber
options.D: Scrub the wound vigorously with povidone-iodine

explanation: Purulent drainage combined with separation indicates infection and compromised healing, requiring medical evaluation before any sutures are disturbed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h3)

question: Which instrument is specifically designed to slide beneath a suture thread during removal?

options.A: Scissors with a small hooked notch
options.B: A blunt-tipped metal hemostat
options.C: A straight-bladed utility scalpel
options.D: Toothe-tipped heavy surgical forceps

explanation: Suture scissors feature a small curved hook or notch that slides easily under the thread to lift and cut it safely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why is normal saline or an appropriate antiseptic used to clean the suture line prior to removal?

options.A: To numb the superficial nerve endings in the skin
options.B: To remove surface crusts and microorganisms
options.C: To chemically dissolve the underlying suture knot
options.D: To permanently seal the epidermal wound margins

explanation: Cleaning clears away dried blood, crusts, and surface bacteria so they are not pulled down into the wound tract during removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h4)

question: When cutting an interrupted suture, why should the nurse pull the cut thread in the direction of the wound?

options.A: To ensure the knot remains attached to the forceps
options.B: To prevent placing stress on the healing incision line
options.C: To push the remaining thread deeper into the subcutaneous tissue
options.D: To stretch the skin and make the removal completely painless

explanation: Pulling toward the wound pushes the edges together rather than pulling them apart, protecting the delicate new tissue from reopening. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What is a major error to avoid when removing any type of suture?

options.A: Cleaning the wound surface with normal saline before cutting
options.B: Using sterile forceps to lift the knot away from the skin
options.C: Pulling the exposed external part of the thread back through the tissue
options.D: Cutting only one side of the suture loop before pulling

explanation: The portion of the suture outside the skin collects bacteria; pulling it through the tissue tract introduces those contaminants directly into the wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h5)

question: What simple material is often applied across an incision after suture removal to provide extra mechanical support?

options.A: Sterile adhesive closure strips
options.B: Heavy waterproof gauze packing
options.C: Zinc oxide medicated tape
options.D: Elastic compression bandages

explanation: Adhesive strips help bridge the wound margins and support the tissue while collagen remodeling continues after sutures are gone. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What instruction is most important for a patient immediately following suture removal?

options.A: Keep the wound clean and dry for the next day or two
options.B: Apply an antiseptic ointment and cover with a heavy occlusive seal
options.C: Return to heavy weightlifting exercises to test the wound
options.D: Apply vigorous friction massage to break down scar tissue

explanation: Keeping the area dry prevents moisture from softening the delicate new epithelial seal and inviting secondary bacterial contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the appropriate immediate nursing response if a wound begins to gape while sutures are being removed?

options.A: Quickly pull out all remaining sutures to finish the task
options.B: Suture the wound back together using a standard needle
options.C: Stop removing remaining sutures and apply adhesive strips
options.D: Leave the clinic without documenting the complication

explanation: Stopping prevents further wound disruption, and applying bridging strips supports the remaining closed margins until a clinician assesses the site. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a classic sign of localized wound infection following suture removal?

options.A: New purulent discharge along the incision
options.B: Cool, pale, and insensible skin edges
options.C: Spreading warmth and localized erythema
options.D: Elevated body temperature in the patient

explanation: Infection typically causes increased warmth, redness (erythema), pus, and fever rather than cool, pale skin. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T12#GNS122_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the primary advantage of parenteral medication administration over the oral route?

options.A: Faster absorption into the bloodstream
options.B: Reduced cost of medical equipment
options.C: Elimination of the need for sterile technique
options.D: Lower risk of localized tissue trauma

explanation: Bypassing the gastrointestinal tract allows medications to enter the circulation and tissues directly for a rapid onset of action. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which action demonstrates the correct application of safe medication principles prior to an injection?

options.A: Preparing medications for several patients simultaneously to save time
options.B: Verifying the prescription against the patient identity band multiple times
options.C: Relying entirely on family members to confirm drug allergies
options.D: Omitting hand hygiene if clean examination gloves are worn

explanation: Cross-checking the medication order with patient identifiers directly prevents administration errors in clinical practice. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h1)

question: Which injection site is currently recommended as the safest choice for intramuscular injections in adults?

options.A: Rectus femoris
options.B: Deltoid
options.C: Ventrogluteal
options.D: Dorsogluteal

explanation: The ventrogluteal site lacks major nerves and blood vessels, minimizing the risk of severe complications during deep muscle injections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: Why is the vastus lateralis muscle selected as the primary injection site for newborns and infants?

options.A: It is a large, well-developed muscle mass free of major nerve trunks.
options.B: It absorbs oily solutions faster than any other muscle group.
options.C: It is the only site that accepts volumes exceeding three milliliters.
options.D: It allows the infant to remain in a prone position easily.

explanation: Infants lack sufficient muscle mass in the gluteal and deltoid regions, making the thick thigh muscle the safest alternative. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h2)

question: What is the standard insertion angle for an intradermal skin test?

options.A: 5 to 15 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 60 degrees
options.D: 45 degrees

explanation: A shallow insertion angle ensures the medication remains within the dermal layer to form a visible bleb. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: A patient requires a routine subcutaneous injection of insulin. Which angle and tissue depth combination is most appropriate?

options.A: Forty-five to ninety degrees into adipose tissue
options.B: Thirty degrees into a peripheral surface vein
options.C: Ninety degrees directly into deep muscle fibers
options.D: Fifteen degrees parallel to the epidermal surface

explanation: Subcutaneous injections target the fat layer beneath the dermis, utilizing a perpendicular or slightly angled approach depending on needle length and patient habitus. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h3)

question: Which needle gauge indicates the largest physical diameter?

options.A: 27 gauge
options.B: 21 gauge
options.C: 18 gauge
options.D: 25 gauge

explanation: Needle gauge operates on an inverse scale, where smaller numbers represent wider bores designed for rapid flow or viscous liquids. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of engineered safety devices on injection needles?

options.A: To filter microscopic glass particles out of reconstituted drugs
options.B: To minimize accidental needlestick injuries for healthcare workers
options.C: To reduce the pain experienced by patients during skin puncture
options.D: To prevent the medication from leaking out of the syringe barrel

explanation: Safety shields and retractable designs physically block or cover the contaminated sharp immediately after use. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h4)

question: What specialized equipment should be used when drawing medication from a glass ampoule to protect the patient?

options.A: Filter needle
options.B: Winged infusion set
options.C: Tuberculin syringe barrel
options.D: Wide-bore 18-gauge needle

explanation: A filter needle traps microscopic glass shards that break off when snapping open an ampoule, preventing them from entering the syringe. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h5)

question: Why must air be injected into a closed medication vial prior to withdrawing the fluid?

options.A: To activate the chemical properties of the powdered drug
options.B: To sterilize the rubber diaphragm from surface bacteria
options.C: To aerate the solution and eliminate trapped bubbles
options.D: To create positive pressure that makes withdrawal easier

explanation: Injecting air replaces the volume of liquid being removed, preventing a vacuum from forming inside the rigid vial. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h5)

question: What is the correct action regarding skin antisepsis before inserting a needle?

options.A: Wipe the wet antiseptic away immediately with sterile gauze.
options.B: Apply the antiseptic in a back-and-forth scrubbing motion.
options.C: Blow forcefully on the skin to accelerate the drying process.
options.D: Allow the antiseptic to air-dry completely before puncture.

explanation: Antiseptics require adequate drying time to destroy surface microorganisms effectively and prevent chemical irritation upon insertion. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: A student nurse prepares to administer an intramuscular injection. What is the correct technique for skin preparation at the selected site?

options.A: Wipe the area horizontally across the muscle fibers three separate times.
options.B: Cleanse in a circular motion starting from the center and moving outward.
options.C: Scrub vigorously from the outer edges toward the center injection spot.
options.D: Soak the skin surface with povidone-iodine for exactly five minutes.

explanation: Moving from the clean center to the dirtier periphery sweeps microorganisms away from the intended puncture site. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h6)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of using the Z-track technique during an intramuscular injection?

options.A: To allow administration of larger volumes than the muscle can hold
options.B: To accelerate the systemic absorption rate of viscous oily solutions
options.C: To eliminate the need for skin antisepsis over bony prominences
options.D: To seal irritating medications deep within the muscle and prevent leakage

explanation: Displacing the skin prior to insertion creates a zigzag track that traps staining or irritating drugs within muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h7)

question: When should the displaced skin be released during a Z-track intramuscular injection?

options.A: Immediately before pushing the plunger to deliver the medication
options.B: After the needle has been completely withdrawn from the tissue
options.C: Before cleansing the skin surface with the alcoholic swab
options.D: While the needle is still resting inside the deep muscle layer

explanation: Releasing the skin only after needle withdrawal ensures the tissue shifts back and seals the needle tract completely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h7)

question: What dangerous practice is a primary contributor to accidental occupational needlestick injuries?

options.A: Manual two-handed recapping of used needles
options.B: Disposing of uncapped sharps in rigid containers
options.C: Washing exposed skin with soap and running water
options.D: Using engineered safety shields on syringes

explanation: Trying to recap used needles with both hands frequently leads to accidental punctures of the fingers and palms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: Which nursing action is most effective in preventing localized muscle fibrosis and tissue necrosis in chronic injection patients?

options.A: Systematic rotation of injection sites across different anatomical zones
options.B: Always using the smallest gauge needle available on the hospital ward
options.C: Injecting medications rapidly to minimize exposure time in the tissue
options.D: Omitting skin antisepsis to prevent chemical irritation of the dermis

explanation: Rotating sites gives damaged tissue adequate time to heal, preventing fibrous scar tissue accumulation and poor drug absorption. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h8)

question: What critical details must be included in the nursing documentation after administering an injection?

options.A: Patient financial status and insurance verification numbers
options.B: Medication name, dose, route, site, date, time, and signature
options.C: The exact brand name of the antiseptic swab used on the skin
options.D: Detailed manufacturer serial numbers of the syringe barrel

explanation: Complete documentation proves that the medication was administered safely according to professional and legal standards. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h9)

question: Why is immediate post-procedure patient monitoring particularly vital after administering a first-time antibiotic injection?

options.A: To detect acute hypersensitivity reactions and life-threatening anaphylaxis early
options.B: To confirm that the patient can swallow oral medications independently
options.C: To measure the exact reduction in body temperature within five minutes
options.D: To prevent the patient from walking around the ward too quickly

explanation: Severe allergic reactions can develop rapidly after parenteral drug exposure, requiring immediate emergency intervention. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T13#GNS122_U2_T13_h9)

question: What is the primary physiological purpose of placing a surgical drain?

options.A: To replace the need for routine systemic antibiotics
options.B: To deliver direct intravenous fluids to the wound
options.C: To evacuate unwanted fluids and prevent dead space
options.D: To speed up the re-epithelialization of skin edges

explanation: Drains remove accumulated blood, serum, or pus that would otherwise create dead space and foster bacterial growth. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h1)

question: Why might a prophylactic drain be placed during an abdominal surgery?

options.A: To eliminate the need for postoperative vital sign monitoring
options.B: To provide a route for enteral feeding directly to the bowel
options.C: To prevent anticipated fluid collections and reduce infection risk
options.D: To permanently replace the function of the patient's kidneys

explanation: Prophylactic drains are placed when surgeons anticipate fluid or blood accumulation that could impair healing or cause infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h1)

question: Which drainage system relies primarily on capillary action rather than mechanical suction?

options.A: Jackson-Pratt drain
options.B: Water-seal chest tube
options.C: Hemovac drain
options.D: Penrose drain

explanation: A Penrose drain is an open, soft rubber tube that uses capillary action to pull fluid along its outer surface onto dressings. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h2)

question: How does a Jackson-Pratt reservoir achieve negative pressure?

options.A: By manual compression of the bulb before closing the port
options.B: By attaching the unit to continuous wall suction
options.C: By positioning the collection chamber below floor level
options.D: By utilizing gravity through a vertical hanging stand

explanation: Squeezing the bulb expels air, and as the plastic attempts to spring back to its original shape, it creates a closed suction force. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h2)

question: What is a critical action when positioning a closed suction drainage reservoir?

options.A: Hanging the reservoir above the level of the patient's head
options.B: Keeping the unit below the level of the insertion site
options.C: Clamping the tubing continuously during patient mobilization
options.D: Taping the collection bulb securely to the surgical incision

explanation: Gravity and proper suction mechanics require the reservoir to stay below the wound to prevent retrograde fluid flow back into the body. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: A nurse notices a sharp kink in a patient's silicone drainage tube. What is the immediate priority?

options.A: Immediately pull the drain out two centimeters to relieve pressure
options.B: Document the finding and wait for the surgeon's morning round
options.C: Instill sterile water down the lumen to push the kink out
options.D: Gently untangle and straighten the tubing without pulling

explanation: Straightening kinks restores patency and allows proper fluid evacuation without risking trauma or premature tube removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h3)

question: What term describes wound drainage that is pale, pink, and watery?

options.A: Biliard
options.B: Purulent
options.C: Sanguineous
options.D: Serosanguineous

explanation: Serosanguineous drainage consists of a mixture of clear serum and red blood cells, commonly seen in healing surgical wounds. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: A patient with an active abdominal drain suddenly stops producing fluid over a four-hour window, despite having steady output prior. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Tubing occlusion or kinking
options.B: Spontaneous internal reabsorption of blood
options.C: Complete surgical healing of the tissue bed
options.D: Systemic dehydration from fluid restriction

explanation: Abrupt cessation of output usually points to mechanical obstruction like a blood clot or kink rather than sudden internal healing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h4)

question: Which direction should cleaning proceed during a drain site dressing change?

options.A: In a vigorous back-and-forth motion across the entire wound
options.B: Only along the vertical axis of the anchoring suture
options.C: From the insertion site outward in a circular motion
options.D: From the outer skin edges inward toward the drain site

explanation: Cleaning from the cleanest area (the wound/tube interface) outward prevents dragging external skin bacteria into the insertion tract. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h5)

question: Why is it vital to change a damp drain dressing promptly?

options.A: Damp gauze increases systemic blood pressure
options.B: Wet dressings dissolve the anchor sutures holding the tube
options.C: Moisture acts as a medium for bacterial proliferation
options.D: Moisture completely stops the suction mechanism

explanation: Warm, damp environments encourage bacterial growth, dramatically raising the risk of local surgical site infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h5)

question: A nurse discovers that a surgical drain has slipped outward by three centimeters. What action is contraindicated?

options.A: Applying a sterile, dry dressing over the insertion site
options.B: Assessing the patient's vital signs for baseline changes
options.C: Notifying the primary surgical team immediately
options.D: Pushing the exposed tubing back into the wound cavity

explanation: Pushing a retracted tube back inside introduces contaminated external tubing and skin bacteria deep into sterile tissues. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h6)

question: What is the primary reason a closed suction bulb fails to maintain negative pressure?

options.A: An open or loosely fitted plug on the evacuation port
options.B: Securing the drainage tubing to the patient's bedsheet
options.C: Placing the collection reservoir below mattress level
options.D: An excessive daily volume of serosanguineous output

explanation: For suction to hold, the system must be completely airtight; an open drainage port allows air to enter and destroys the vacuum. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h6)

question: What breathing instruction is typically given to a patient right as a surgical drain is pulled out?

options.A: Hold your breath and bear down continuously
options.B: Take a deep breath and hold it
options.C: Cough forcefully to push out remaining fluid
options.D: Breathe in and out rapidly through the mouth

explanation: Holding a breath (or performing a Valsalva maneuver) increases intrathoracic or intra-abdominal pressure, preventing air entry and easing removal. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h7)

question: Which clinical finding generally indicates that a surgical drain is ready for removal?

options.A: The patient reports mild itching around the adhesive tape
options.B: The surrounding skin shows signs of minor bruising
options.C: The external collection bulb maintains negative pressure for 48 hours
options.D: Daily output decreases below the surgeon's threshold limit

explanation: Drains are discontinued when fluid output drops to minimal levels (such as under 30 mL/day), indicating the cavity is healing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of implementing isolation techniques in a clinical setting?

options.A: To permanently eliminate all bacteria from the hospital ward
options.B: To interrupt the transmission of pathogenic microorganisms
options.C: To accelerate the pharmacological recovery of the patient
options.D: To substitute for standard hand hygiene practices

explanation: Isolation creates physical barriers specifically to stop pathogens from spreading to other patients, staff, and visitors. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h1)

question: Why are basic barrier methods considered critical in resource-constrained healthcare environments?

options.A: They replace the requirement for systemic antibiotic administration
options.B: They completely eliminate the need for surface disinfection protocols
options.C: They reduce the total length of hospital stay for surgical patients
options.D: They serve as a reliable defense against hospital-acquired infections when supplies are low

explanation: When environmental cleaning supplies or staffing are limited, proper isolation protocols provide a dependable frontline defense against cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h1)

question: Which two links in the chain of infection are most directly disrupted by isolation techniques?

options.A: Reservoir and systemic immune response
options.B: Mode of transmission and portal of exit
options.C: Portal of entry and incubation period
options.D: Infectious agent and host susceptibility

explanation: Barriers like masks, gloves, and private rooms stop pathogens from leaving an infected person and traveling to a new host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: How does understanding the chain of infection assist a nurse during an infectious outbreak?

options.A: It enables the prediction of pathogen spread for targeted barrier defense application
options.B: It determines the appropriate dosage of prophylactic antipyretics
options.C: It identifies the genetic mutation rate of the microorganism
options.D: It calculates the exact mortality rate of the infecting organism

explanation: Recognizing how an organism moves through the links allows nurses to choose the exact interventions needed to halt transmission. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h2)

question: Who must standard precautions be applied to in the clinical environment?

options.A: Only patients with confirmed viral hemorrhagic fevers
options.B: Individuals showing visible symptoms of respiratory distress
options.C: All patients regardless of their infection status
options.D: Patients admitted specifically to the intensive care unit

explanation: Standard precautions assume that every patient's blood and body fluids are potentially infectious, making them universal for all care. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: What is the relationship between standard precautions and transmission-based precautions?

options.A: Transmission-based precautions replace standard care for asymptomatic individuals
options.B: Standard precautions only apply when airborne pathogens are identified
options.C: Standard precautions are discontinued once transmission-based measures begin
options.D: Transmission-based precautions are always implemented in addition to standard precautions

explanation: Specialized transmission-based measures never replace basic safety; they build upon the foundation of standard precautions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h3)

question: Which type of precaution requires the use of a fit-tested N95 respirator mask?

options.A: Standard precautions
options.B: Droplet precautions
options.C: Airborne precautions
options.D: Contact precautions

explanation: Tiny airborne droplet nuclei can remain suspended in the air, requiring specialized respiratory filtration like an N95 mask to prevent inhalation. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: A patient with confirmed pulmonary tuberculosis is admitted to the medical ward. Which room assignment is most appropriate?

options.A: A shared double-occupancy cohort room
options.B: A standard open ward near the nursing station
options.C: A negative pressure isolation room
options.D: A well-ventilated room with open windows

explanation: Tuberculosis spreads via airborne nuclei, necessitating a negative pressure room to prevent contaminated air from escaping into the hallway. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h4)

question: What is the very first item of personal protective equipment that should be removed during the doffing process?

options.A: Respirator mask
options.B: Face shield
options.C: Gown
options.D: Gloves

explanation: Gloves are usually the most contaminated items and are removed first to prevent touching other clean or semi-clean areas of the body. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why is the sequence of donning and doffing personal protective equipment strictly regulated?

options.A: To comply with administrative hospital laundry schedules
options.B: To ensure that the most expensive protective items are used last
options.C: To shorten the time required to prepare for a sterile surgical procedure
options.D: To prevent self-contamination during the removal of hazardous biological agents

explanation: A strict sequence stops infectious material on the outside of used barriers from transferring onto skin, hair, or scrubs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: What term describes the practice of grouping patients infected with the same specific microorganism together in one room?

options.A: Segregating
options.B: Cohorting
options.C: Quarantining
options.D: Sterilizing

explanation: When private rooms are limited, patients with identical confirmed infections are safely housed together, a practice known as cohorting. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: What is the primary function of engineering controls in an isolation strategy?

options.A: Monitoring patient compliance with handwashing protocols
options.B: Using physical building design and ventilation to reduce pathogen circulation
options.C: Replacing the requirement for healthcare workers to wear face masks
options.D: Automatically disinfecting all surface areas without human intervention

explanation: Engineering controls rely on structural elements like negative pressure systems and spatial layouts to physically manage air and space safety. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h6)

question: Which emotional response is most commonly observed in patients subjected to prolonged strict isolation?

options.A: A sudden increase in overall physical strength
options.B: Feelings of alienation and sensory deprivation
options.C: Enhanced cognitive focus and relaxation
options.D: Indifference toward medical treatments and procedures

explanation: Restricted human contact and the sight of masked personnel often lead to psychological withdrawal, loneliness, and anxiety. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h7)

question: A patient on contact precautions appears withdrawn and expresses fear because staff members wear full protective gear. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Limit verbal communication to essential tasks to minimize contact time
options.B: Take time to talk, explain the purpose of the gear, and provide reassurance
options.C: Remove the protective gown before entering to make the patient less anxious
options.D: Reassure the patient that the infection is entirely harmless

explanation: Clear explanations and compassionate, unhurried communication help reduce fear and bridge the emotional gap created by barriers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of barrier nursing?

options.A: To prevent the transmission of infectious agents
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays
options.C: To completely eliminate normal body flora
options.D: To accelerate the wound healing process

explanation: Barrier nursing utilizes physical and procedural blocks specifically to stop pathogens from spreading between patients, staff, and the environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: Why is barrier nursing particularly vital in under-resourced healthcare settings?

options.A: It helps contain outbreaks of highly contagious diseases locally
options.B: It guarantees complete immunity for all attending staff
options.C: It allows hospitals to bypass routine sterilization cycles
options.D: It replaces the need for standard handwashing procedures

explanation: Strict containment protocols prevent localized infectious threats from escalating into widespread nosocomial or community outbreaks when resources are tight. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h1)

question: Which of the following represents the reservoir in the chain of infection?

options.A: The chemical agent used to sterilize surgical instruments
options.B: The specific entry point on a new patient's body
options.C: The natural habitat where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.D: The physical route the microorganism uses to travel

explanation: A reservoir provides the essential conditions for survival and reproduction before the pathogen finds a way to infect a new host. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: Hand hygiene performed by a nurse primarily interrupts which link in the chain of infection?

options.A: Mode of transmission
options.B: Portal of entry
options.C: Infectious agent
options.D: Susceptible host

explanation: Washing hands removes transient microorganisms, preventing the nurse's hands from acting as the vehicle that transfers pathogens between sources. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h2)

question: What is the primary goal of protective or reverse isolation?

options.A: To shield a highly susceptible patient from outside pathogens
options.B: To prevent the spread of gastrointestinal parasites
options.C: To manage patients with severe multi-drug resistant wounds
options.D: To contain a highly contagious airborne virus within a room

explanation: Reverse isolation protects vulnerable, immunocompromised individuals by filtering incoming air and enforcing strict barrier measures on all visitors and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: A patient admitted with suspected Lassa fever requires which category of barrier precaution?

options.A: Strict isolation
options.B: Enteric precautions
options.C: Standard precautions only
options.D: Reverse isolation

explanation: Viral hemorrhagic fevers demand rigorous strict isolation protocols to prevent transmission through contact with body fluids and potential airborne spread. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h3)

question: Who should be cared for using Standard Precautions in the healthcare setting?

options.A: Patients admitted exclusively to intensive care units
options.B: Only individuals showing active respiratory symptoms
options.C: All patients, regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.D: Only patients with confirmed multi-drug resistant infections

explanation: Standard precautions assume that any patient could harbor bloodborne or body fluid pathogens, making them universal across all clinical interactions. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: When are Transmission-Based Precautions initiated for a patient?

options.A: Only after laboratory cultures return positive results after discharge
options.B: Whenever a nurse begins a morning shift in a medical ward
options.C: As a replacement for standard hand hygiene practices
options.D: When a patient is suspected or confirmed to have a specific transmissible pathogen

explanation: Transmission-based precautions are targeted measures added to standard precautions based on clinical presentation or known infection history. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h4)

question: What is the very first item of PPE that should be removed when doffing after patient care?

options.A: Gown
options.B: Gloves
options.C: Face shield
options.D: Respirator mask

explanation: Gloves are typically the most contaminated item and must be removed first to prevent touching other parts of the body or clean PPE with dirty hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: Why must a gown be tied securely and pulled over the cuffs of the gloves during donning?

options.A: To ensure the gown can be easily torn off during an emergency
options.B: To keep the uniform beneath completely wrinkle-free
options.C: To prevent exposed skin gaps at the wrists where pathogens can enter
options.D: To comply with aesthetic hospital uniform standards

explanation: Overlapping glove cuffs onto the gown sleeves creates a continuous barrier, eliminating exposed skin at a highly active joint area. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h5)

question: Which color bag or bin is standard for disposing of infectious biomedical waste in most Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Clear
options.B: Black
options.C: Yellow
options.D: Blue

explanation: Yellow bins and bags are universally designated for infectious, contaminated, and pathological waste requiring incineration or specialized treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: What is the primary danger of failing to follow proper medical waste segregation in an isolation ward?

options.A: Increased financial costs associated with buying colored bin liners
options.B: Exposure of sanitation workers and the community to infectious pathogens
options.C: Slower degradation rates of municipal garbage in local landfills
options.D: Unpleasant odors developing within the administrative offices

explanation: Mixing infectious materials like used syringes into general waste threatens waste handlers and spreads disease outside the hospital walls. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h6)

question: Which psychological response is most commonly observed in patients placed under strict isolation?

options.A: Immediate euphoria and appreciation for privacy
options.B: Complete indifference toward their medical treatment
options.C: Enhanced cognitive focus and reduced fatigue
options.D: Anxiety, depression, and feelings of isolation

explanation: Restricted movement and minimal human contact frequently trigger emotional distress and loneliness in isolated patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: How can a nurse best mitigate the psychological impact of barrier nursing on a hospitalized patient?

options.A: By maintaining regular, empathetic communication and explaining the care plan
options.B: By leaving PPE outside the room to make interactions appear casual
options.C: By assigning all communication tasks exclusively to housekeeping staff
options.D: By completely eliminating visiting hours to ensure uninterrupted sleep

explanation: Frequent communication reassures the patient, reduces fear of the unknown, and preserves their sense of dignity despite physical barriers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h7)

question: What is a primary responsibility of the nurse regarding visitors in an isolation room?

options.A: Allowing unrestricted access to support family bonding
options.B: Asking them to clean the patient's bathroom facilities
options.C: Requiring them to sign a liability waiver for the hospital
options.D: Educating them on proper hand hygiene and PPE use before entry

explanation: Nurses must ensure that every person entering an isolation environment understands and adheres to infection control protocols to prevent pathogen migration. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: A nurse notices a colleague stepping out of an isolation room without removing their contaminated gown. What is the most appropriate initial action?

options.A: Disinfect the hallway floor where the colleague walked
options.B: Ignore the incident to avoid workplace conflict among peers
options.C: Gently remind and assist the colleague on correct doffing procedure
options.D: Report the colleague directly to the hospital board of directors

explanation: Peer-to-peer correction ensures immediate safety compliance while maintaining a supportive, educational professional environment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T16#GNS122_U2_T16_h8)

question: What is the primary goal of aseptic techniques in healthcare settings?

options.A: To treat active systemic infections using broad-spectrum drugs
options.B: To minimize pathogenic microorganisms to prevent infection
options.C: To achieve complete chemical sterilization of the entire room
options.D: To eliminate all normal human flora from the patient's skin

explanation: Aseptic techniques aim to reduce pathogens to a safe level rather than sterilizing entire environments or eradicating resident skin flora. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h1)

question: Why is strict infection control particularly vital in resource-limited healthcare environments?

options.A: It replaces the need for administering therapeutic antibiotics
options.B: It guarantees that patients will never develop chronic illnesses
options.C: It compensates for a total lack of cleaning supplies
options.D: It prevents the amplification and spread of cross-contamination

explanation: Where supplies or infrastructure may be constrained, breaking the chain of infection through reliable technique stops pathogens from spreading between patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which clinical procedure requires the application of surgical asepsis?

options.A: Inserting an indwelling urinary catheter
options.B: Administering an oral liquid medication
options.C: Feeding a client using a nasogastric tube
options.D: Assisting a patient with bed bath hygiene

explanation: Urinary catheterization enters a sterile body cavity, demanding surgical asepsis to prevent introducing pathogens into the bladder. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h2)

question: The fundamental distinction between medical asepsis and surgical asepsis lies in which factor?

options.A: The mandatory requirement of wearing sterile face masks for every procedure
options.B: The total elimination of microorganisms versus reducing their overall number
options.C: The physical location within the hospital where the care is delivered
options.D: The specific type of liquid soap utilized during routine hand hygiene

explanation: Medical asepsis reduces the count and transfer of pathogens, while surgical asepsis ensures total destruction or absence of all microbial life and spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h2)

question: What action must a nurse take if a sterile package falls below the waist level?

options.A: Consider the item contaminated and discard or reprocess it
options.B: Wipe the outer packaging with alcohol and use it immediately
options.C: Open the package cautiously to check if the inner wrap is dry
options.D: Place the item back onto the sterile field if the seal is intact

explanation: Items kept below waist level are out of the immediate visual field and are automatically classified as contaminated. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h3)

question: Why does moisture penetration compromise the integrity of a sterile wrapper?

options.A: It neutralizes the pre-sterilized status by creating toxic gases
options.B: It permanently dissolves the chemical indicators printed on the paper
options.C: It allows microorganisms to travel across the barrier via capillary action
options.D: It causes the inner sterile contents to undergo immediate rusting

explanation: Liquid acts as a wick, drawing bacteria from unsterile surfaces through the damp barrier material onto the sterile field. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h3)

question: When is hand washing with soap and water strictly required over alcohol-based hand rubs?

options.A: Before touching a patient who has an intact skin barrier
options.B: Whenever entering a general medical ward in the morning
options.C: Immediately after checking a patient's blood pressure cuff
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Visible organic material and certain non-enveloped or spore-forming pathogens require the mechanical friction and rinsing action of soap and water. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the primary risk associated with removing personal protective equipment incorrectly?

options.A: Permanently damaging the specialized fibers of the protective gown
options.B: Invalidating the sterile inventory count recorded in the treatment room
options.C: Causing immediate chemical irritation to the clinician's respiratory tract
options.D: Transferring pathogens from contaminated outer surfaces to skin or scrubs

explanation: Improper doffing techniques often result in infectious material touching the wearer's skin, hair, or clean clothing, defeating the purpose of the barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h4)

question: In what direction should the first flap of a wrapped sterile package be opened?

options.A: Directly toward the chest of the healthcare provider
options.B: In a downward circular motion toward the floor
options.C: To the left side, parallel to the edge of the table
options.D: Away from the body of the person opening the package

explanation: Opening the first flap away from the body prevents arms and hands from reaching over the sterile contents inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is it unacceptable to leave an established sterile field unattended?

options.A: Sterile instruments will lose their metallic temper if left alone
options.B: Unseen contamination may occur and go unrecognized by the nurse
options.C: The sterile drapes will automatically slide off the tabletop
options.D: Hospital administrative policies require constant video recording

explanation: An unattended field leaves room for accidental contamination by others, drafts, or dust, compromising patient safety if used unknowingly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h5)

question: Which processing method completely eliminates all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores?

options.A: High-level disinfection
options.B: Routine surface cleaning
options.C: Antiseptic scrubbing
options.D: Sterilization

explanation: Sterilization is the only process that destroys all microorganisms, including highly resistant bacterial endospores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h6)

question: A clinic nurse needs to process heat-sensitive fiberoptic endoscopes. Which technique is most appropriate?

options.A: High-pressure steam autoclaving at maximum temperature
options.B: Routine wiping with plain water and liquid dish soap
options.C: High-level chemical disinfection using immersion solutions
options.D: Dry heat oven baking for an extended overnight cycle

explanation: Delicate endoscopes damaged by high heat require high-level disinfection via chemical agents like glutaraldehyde rather than steam sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h6)

question: What is a primary clinical source of many healthcare-associated bloodstream infections?

options.A: Routine oral medication administration cups
options.B: Indwelling vascular access devices and central lines
options.C: Standard hospital room privacy curtains
options.D: Non-invasive blood pressure cuff monitoring

explanation: Vascular catheters bypass natural skin defenses, serving as direct entry points for pathogens into the bloodstream if not maintained aseptically. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended strategy for actively reducing healthcare-associated infections?

options.A: Reusing single-use disposable syringes after chemical rinsing
options.B: Monitoring surgical sites for early signs of localized inflammation
options.C: Performing reliable hand hygiene before and after patient contact
options.D: Implementing strict evidence-based insertion and care bundles

explanation: Single-use devices must never be reused; attempting to clean and reuse them introduces severe infection risks and violates core safety standards. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h7)

question: To which group of patients do standard precautions apply in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Patients admitted to surgical wards exclusively
options.B: Only patients diagnosed with blood-borne viruses
options.C: Individuals exhibiting active respiratory symptoms
options.D: All patients receiving care regardless of infection status

explanation: Standard precautions are designed to be applied universally to every patient encounter to minimize transmission risks from unrecognized pathogen sources. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: What is the primary assumption underlying the implementation of standard precautions?
