options.A: Healthy individuals carry no risk of shedding microbial agents
options.B: All body fluids and moist tissues are potentially infectious
options.C: Infection transmission only occurs through airborne droplets
options.D: Only visible blood contains transmissible viral pathogens

explanation: Treating all moist body substances as hazardous eliminates the dangerous gamble of guessing who is infected based on outward appearance. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h1)

question: When is handwashing with soap and water strictly required over alcohol rub?

options.A: Following the routine measurement of a patient's blood pressure
options.B: Immediately before applying sterile surgical gloves
options.C: At the beginning of every nursing shift change
options.D: When hands are visibly soiled with dirt or body fluids

explanation: Friction from soap and water is physically necessary to remove gross organic soil and certain non-enveloped spores that alcohol rubs cannot destroy effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: Why must hand hygiene still be performed immediately after removing medical gloves?

options.A: Gloves can develop microscopic defects and permit pathogen passage
options.B: Hand lotion applied earlier is wiped away during glove removal
options.C: Hospital accreditation standards require a double-wash routine
options.D: Powder inside the gloves stimulates excessive bacterial growth

explanation: Tiny punctures or tears often occur during patient care tasks, allowing microbes to colonize the skin surface despite the glove barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the correct sequence for putting on full personal protective equipment?

options.A: Goggles, gloves, gown, respiratory mask
options.B: Gown, mask or respirator, goggles or face shield, gloves
options.C: Gloves, gown, face shield, surgical mask
options.D: Mask, gloves, protective gown, eye wear

explanation: Donning begins with the gown to cover the body, followed by respiratory protection, eye protection, and gloves pulled up over the gown cuffs last. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing to irrigate a contaminated wound that is expected to splash fluid. Which combination of protective gear is most appropriate?

options.A: N95 respirator mask and sterile shoe covers only
options.B: Sterile gloves and a standard short-sleeved clinical uniform
options.C: Gloves, fluid-resistant gown, mask, and eye protection
options.D: Disposable plastic apron and clean examination gloves

explanation: Wound irrigation generates high-risk splashes, requiring full barrier coverage for hands, clothing, respiratory tract, and mucous membranes of the eyes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the immediate action an individual should take after coughing into a tissue?

options.A: Wipe down surrounding chairs with an antiseptic wipe
options.B: Leave the tissue on the nearest flat surface for housekeeping
options.C: Discard the tissue and perform hand hygiene
options.D: Fold the tissue and place it inside a uniform pocket

explanation: Immediate disposal and hand cleansing prevent infectious respiratory droplets from transferring to hands and environmental surfaces. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Why is respiratory hygiene considered a source-control measure in standard precautions?

options.A: It filters ambient room air before it reaches the patient's lungs
options.B: It destroys airborne bacterial spores through chemical vaporization
options.C: It captures infectious droplets directly at the point of release
options.D: It eliminates the need for nurses to wear surgical face masks

explanation: Source control intercepts pathogens before they travel into the surrounding environment or contaminate other individuals nearby. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which practice is strictly prohibited when handling used hollow-bore needles?

options.A: Recapping needles using a two-handed manual technique
options.B: Placing the unrecapped syringe directly into a puncture-resistant bin
options.C: Carrying the used syringe tray to the bedside treatment cart
options.D: Activating built-in safety engineered needle devices immediately

explanation: Two-handed recapping drastically elevates the risk of accidental needle-stick injuries to the fingers and hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: At what point should a clinical sharps container be securely closed and replaced?

options.A: After every single patient injection procedure is finished
options.B: Only at the official end of each nursing shift rotation
options.C: When the outside container surface appears dusty or stained
options.D: When the contents reach the designated fill line indicator

explanation: Overfilling sharps containers crowds the opening and exposes personnel handling the waste to protruding needles. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h5)

question: How should soiled bed linens be handled to minimize environmental contamination?

options.A: Rolled inward and placed directly into a designated laundry bag
options.B: Folded neatly on the bedside table for reuse on the next patient
options.C: Draped over hallway chairs until housekeeping arrives to collect them
options.D: Shaken vigorously in the open ward to remove loose debris

explanation: Rolling linens inward traps organic soil and prevents pathogenic dust from scattering into the breathing zone of staff and patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: Which surface category in a patient room requires the most frequent routine disinfection?

options.A: Ceiling tiles and upper wall ventilation grilles
options.B: The underneath framework of the patient mattress
options.C: Window glass panels facing exterior courtyards
options.D: High-touch surfaces like bed rails and call buttons

explanation: Frequent hand contact makes high-touch objects primary vehicles for transmitting hospital-acquired infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the initial emergency action a nurse must take following a contaminated needle-stick injury?

options.A: Squeeze the finger tightly to expel trapped venous blood
options.B: Apply an alcohol-based tincture directly inside the wound
options.C: Wait until the end of the shift to report the event
options.D: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and water

explanation: Immediate washing reduces the viral or bacterial load entering the bloodstream through the open wound. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: Which action should NOT be performed when managing an accidental skin puncture from a used needle?

options.A: Documenting the precise details of the exposure event
options.B: Aggressively squeezing or milking the wound to force out blood
options.C: Flushing the exposed skin area with clean running water
options.D: Reporting the incident promptly to the facility health officer

explanation: Squeezing or milking damages delicate local tissues and can actually increase micro-vascular absorption of infectious pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h7)

question: What is the primary objective of the sterilization process?

options.A: Reduction of visible dirt and organic matter from surfaces
options.B: Destruction of vegetative bacteria while leaving spores intact
options.C: Inactivation of common viruses on non-critical furniture
options.D: Complete elimination of all microbial life including spores

explanation: Sterilization is the highest level of microbial control, designed to destroy every living organism and resistant spore present on an object. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why is achieving basic cleaning insufficient for surgical instruments entering the bloodstream?

options.A: Cleaning agents leave toxic residues that irritate healthy human tissue
options.B: Residual spores and microorganisms can directly seed severe systemic infections
options.C: Washing processes destroy the metallic integrity of sharp cutting blades
options.D: Blood proteins become permanently bonded to steel during washing

explanation: Instruments breaching sterile tissues require absolute freedom from all microbes to prevent introducing pathogens directly into internal body sites. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h1)

question: Which decontamination process must always precede both disinfection and sterilization?

options.A: High-pressure steam autoclaving
options.B: Thorough cleaning and washing
options.C: Chemical immersion in glutaraldehyde
options.D: Ultraviolet surface radiation

explanation: Organic soil acts as a protective barrier for microorganisms and must be physically washed away before disinfectants or sterilants can work effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: What primary feature separates disinfection from sterilization?

options.A: Disinfection is performed exclusively with boiling water
options.B: Disinfection is only used for non-reusable plastic items
options.C: Sterilization completely destroys resistant bacterial spores
options.D: Sterilization requires no prior equipment preparation

explanation: While disinfection eliminates most vegetative pathogens, only true sterilization reliably destroys tough bacterial endospores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which category of instruments requires complete sterilization according to the Spaulding classification?

options.A: Semi-critical items
options.B: Critical items
options.C: Environmental items
options.D: Non-critical items

explanation: Critical items break the skin barrier or enter sterile cavities, carrying the highest risk of infection and requiring full sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing a flexible gastrointestinal endoscope for a patient procedure. Based on the Spaulding classification, how should this device be processed?

options.A: Low-level disinfection using quaternary ammonium compounds
options.B: Simple washing with ordinary tap water and soap
options.C: Immediate high-pressure steam autoclaving for twenty minutes
options.D: High-level disinfection or sterilization due to mucous membrane contact

explanation: Endoscopes touch mucous membranes, classifying them as semi-critical devices that require high-level disinfection or sterilization to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the standard time and temperature combination for gravity displacement steam autoclaving?

options.A: 160°C in dry air for 3 hours
options.B: 134°C with chemical vapors for 5 minutes
options.C: 121°C at 15 psi for 15 to 30 minutes
options.D: 100°C at atmospheric pressure for 60 minutes

explanation: The classic parameters of 121°C, 15 pounds per square inch of pressure, and sufficient time ensure steam penetrates packages and destroys all spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: When is dry heat sterilization preferred over steam autoclaving in clinical settings?

options.A: For oils, powders, and moisture-sensitive sharp instruments
options.B: For large bundles of surgical linen and cotton drapes
options.C: For rubber tubing and flexible plastic catheters
options.D: For hollow lumened needles requiring rapid turnaround

explanation: Dry heat does not rust carbon steel and can penetrate non-aqueous powders and oils where steam cannot reach effectively. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h4)

question: Which chemical agent is frequently used for liquid immersion sterilization or high-level disinfection of heat-sensitive scopes?

options.A: Glutaraldehyde
options.B: Chlorhexidine gluconate
options.C: Normal saline
options.D: Isopropyl rubbing alcohol

explanation: Glutaraldehyde is a powerful chemical sterilant and disinfectant commonly used for immersible heat-sensitive medical devices. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: What is a major clinical limitation associated with using liquid chemical sterilants for surgical instruments?

options.A: Items often require sterile rinsing which can re-introduce contaminants if care is lacking
options.B: They demand extreme high-pressure chambers similar to steam autoclaves
options.C: They instantly melt stainless steel surfaces at room temperature
options.D: They require lengthy aeration to eliminate toxic chemical residues

explanation: Unlike terminal steam sterilization inside a sealed wrapper, chemical immersion usually requires rinsing with sterile water post-treatment, risking touch contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h5)

question: Which type of monitoring indicator provides direct microbiological proof that sterilization conditions successfully destroyed resistant bacterial spores?

options.A: Chemical indicator tape
options.B: External temperature charts
options.C: Mechanical pressure gauges
options.D: Biological indicators

explanation: Biological indicators use actual bacterial spores to test the lethality of the sterilization cycle, offering the highest level of quality assurance. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What is the limitation of relying solely on external chemical indicator tape on a wrapped instrument pack?

options.A: It can only be read accurately using an ultraviolet laboratory microscope
options.B: It automatically turns black whenever humidity in the room rises above normal levels
options.C: It permanently melts if the autoclave chamber reaches overpressure
options.D: It only proves the exterior was exposed to heat or steam, not that internal items reached required conditions

explanation: Chemical indicator tape confirms exposure to a variable like heat, but it does not guarantee that steam penetrated deep inside the pack to kill all internal spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h6)

question: What modern principle determines whether a stored sterile package is safe to use rather than relying on a fixed calendar expiration date?

options.A: Atmospheric humidity tracking
options.B: Absolute shelf-life timing
options.C: Event-related sterility
options.D: Daily mandatory re-autoclaving

explanation: Sterility is maintained based on package handling and environmental integrity (events) rather than the passage of time on a calendar. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: A nurse notices that a sterile instrument pack has accidentally fallen onto a damp hospital floor. What action is required?

options.A: Inspect the wrapper for tears, and if intact, use it immediately for the next patient
options.B: Wipe the outer wrapper with alcohol and store it back on the shelf
options.C: Consider the package compromised due to moisture and contamination, requiring complete re-sterilization
options.D: Send the pack directly to the laboratory for biological spore testing

explanation: Moisture allows microorganisms to wick through packaging material via a process called strike-through, rendering the contents unsterile regardless of visual appearance. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T4#GNS122_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of disinfection in a clinical setting?

options.A: Eliminating all microbial life including bacterial spores
options.B: Preventing colonization on intact human skin
options.C: Removing visible organic soil from surgical instruments
options.D: Destroying or inactivating pathogens on inanimate surfaces

explanation: Disinfection specifically targets pathogens on inanimate objects or surfaces to prevent cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: Why is disinfection considered a core pillar of infection control for nurses?

options.A: It completely eliminates the risk of airborne transmission in wards
options.B: It interrupts the chain of transmission by neutralizing environmental reservoirs
options.C: It replaces the need for standard hand hygiene protocols between patients
options.D: It permanently sterilizes surgical instruments for immediate invasive reuse

explanation: Infectious agents often persist on hospital surfaces, making environmental disinfection essential for stopping transmission to vulnerable patients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which process achieves the complete destruction of all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores?

options.A: Cleaning
options.B: Sanitization
options.C: Disinfection
options.D: Sterilization

explanation: Sterilization is the only process among the choices that guarantees the complete elimination of all microbial life, including bacterial endospores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: What is the primary limitation of disinfection compared to sterilization?

options.A: Disinfection only removes visible organic soil and dust
options.B: Disinfection typically fails to eliminate bacterial spores
options.C: Disinfection can only be performed on human skin
options.D: Disinfection requires high-pressure steam autoclaves

explanation: While disinfection destroys most vegetative pathogens, bacterial spores possess high resistance and usually survive standard chemical disinfection processes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h2)

question: Which level of disinfection is required for semi-critical items such as flexible gastrointestinal endoscopes?

options.A: Low-level disinfection
options.B: High-level disinfection
options.C: Intermediate-level disinfection
options.D: Routine cleaning only

explanation: Semi-critical items touch mucous membranes or non-intact skin and require high-level disinfection to destroy all microorganisms except high numbers of spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: A patient care item comes into contact only with intact skin. What level of disinfection is generally appropriate?

options.A: High-level disinfection
options.B: Chemical pasteurization
options.C: Low-level disinfection
options.D: Complete sterilization

explanation: Non-critical items that touch only intact skin pose a low risk of infection and typically require only low-level disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanism by which alcohol-based disinfectants destroy microorganisms?

options.A: Releasing toxic ethylene oxide gas molecules
options.B: Generating high-pressure steam inside cell walls
options.C: Coagulating proteins and dissolving lipid membranes
options.D: Selectively blocking human nerve transmission

explanation: Alcohols rapidly denature proteins and disrupt the lipid cell membranes of many bacteria and viruses. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h4)

question: Why does the rapid evaporation of alcohol limit its effectiveness as a surface disinfectant?

options.A: It reduces the necessary contact time needed to neutralize pathogens
options.B: It neutralizes the detergent properties required to lift organic soil
options.C: It causes immediate corrosion of stainless steel hospital beds
options.D: It converts the liquid solution directly into hazardous toxic gas

explanation: Disinfectants require a specific wet contact time to successfully destroy pathogens; fast evaporation can cause surfaces to dry too quickly. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h4)

question: What is the primary negative effect of organic matter, such as blood or mucus, on chemical disinfection?

options.A: It permanently lowers the ambient room temperature
options.B: It converts low-level disinfectants directly into sterilizing agents
options.C: It accelerates the evaporation rate of alcohol-based solutions
options.D: It acts as a physical barrier and binds to the chemical agent

explanation: Organic soil protects microorganisms from contact with the disinfectant and can neutralize active chemical ingredients. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h5)

question: A nurse wipes down a treatment table with a chlorine solution but dries the surface immediately instead of letting it air dry. What is the most likely consequence?

options.A: The chemical solution will permanently etch the tabletop
options.B: The disinfectant will spontaneously transform into pure water
options.C: Inadequate contact time reduces the antimicrobial efficacy
options.D: Bacterial spores will immediately multiply into vegetative cells

explanation: Disinfectants need adequate wet contact time to penetrate and destroy microbial cells; wiping them off prematurely compromises disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h5)

question: What is the correct procedural order when processing a heavily soiled reusable non-critical medical item?

options.A: Clean with detergent and water first, then apply the appropriate disinfectant
options.B: Immerge the item directly into boiling water without prior washing
options.C: Apply high-level chemical disinfection first, then scrub off the remaining soil
options.D: Spray alcohol over the organic matter and wipe away immediately

explanation: Organic soil must be physically cleaned and removed before disinfection because debris inactivates chemical agents. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why should nurses wipe clinical surfaces in a directional pattern from clean to dirty areas?

options.A: To prevent the formation of toxic gas mixtures during wiping
options.B: To accelerate the chemical evaporation rate across the surface
options.C: To ensure equal distribution of detergent foam across the floor
options.D: To avoid spreading contaminants to previously decontaminated zones

explanation: Moving from clean to dirty areas prevents dragging pathogens across sanitized surfaces, maintaining a true barrier against cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h6)

question: Which document must be readily accessible in clinical units to inform nurses about the hazards and safe handling of specific disinfectants?

options.A: Hospital Budget Report
options.B: Nursing Care Plan Template
options.C: Patient Admission Log
options.D: Safety Data Sheet

explanation: Safety Data Sheets provide vital information regarding chemical hazards, protective equipment, and emergency response procedures for handling disinfectants. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended safety precaution when handling strong chemical disinfectants in a utility room?

options.A: Performing tasks in an unventilated, enclosed small closet
options.B: Wearing appropriate chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
options.C: Referencing product instructions for correct dilution ratios
options.D: Ensuring eyewash stations are operational and unobstructed

explanation: Strong disinfectants emit fumes that require good ventilation; working in an unventilated space risks respiratory irritation and toxicity. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T5#GNS122_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of decontamination in a clinical setting?

options.A: To remove visible dirt and improve the aesthetic appearance of equipment
options.B: To remove or destroy pathogens and prevent infection transmission
options.C: To extend the physical lifespan of delicate metallic instruments
options.D: To neutralize toxic chemical waste produced during surgery

explanation: Decontamination specifically targets microorganisms to stop the spread of infection to patients and staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Why is proper decontamination critical in under-resourced healthcare facilities?

options.A: It shortens the recovery time of patients admitted with severe sepsis
options.B: It compensates for a lack of running water by using chemical sprays
options.C: It prevents hospitals from becoming reservoirs for resistant pathogens
options.D: It eliminates the need for purchasing any disposable medical supplies

explanation: Resource-limited settings often face high infection burdens, making rigorous decontamination vital to stop cross-contamination. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h1)

question: Which processing method destroys all forms of microbial life, including bacterial spores?

options.A: Disinfection
options.B: Cleaning
options.C: Sanitization
options.D: Sterilization

explanation: Only sterilization achieves the complete destruction of every microbial form, including resilient spores. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Why must thorough cleaning always be performed before disinfection or sterilization?

options.A: Detergents lower the weight of the instruments for easier autoclaving
options.B: Organic debris can protect and shield microorganisms from chemical agents
options.C: Dry blood makes metallic surfaces completely immune to rust
options.D: Cleaning agents instantly sterilize the instruments on contact

explanation: Blood, protein, and bodily fluids act as a physical barrier that prevents disinfectants and heat from reaching underlying pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: Which Spaulding classification requires absolute sterilization before patient use?

options.A: Critical items
options.B: Non-critical items
options.C: Semi-critical items
options.D: Environmental items

explanation: Critical items enter sterile body cavities and the vascular system, necessitating complete sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: A nurse is preparing a vaginal speculum for reuse on another patient. According to the Spaulding classification, this item is classified as:

options.A: Sterile
options.B: Semi-critical
options.C: Non-critical
options.D: Critical

explanation: Vaginal specula touch mucous membranes without penetrating sterile tissue, placing them in the semi-critical category. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h3)

question: What is the very first step that should be taken with surgical instruments immediately after a procedure is completed?

options.A: Immediate high-pressure steam sterilization in the operating room
options.B: Point-of-use removal of gross soil and keeping them moist
options.C: Submerging the instruments in concentrated bleach for 24 hours
options.D: Packaging the items tightly in cloth wrappers for transport

explanation: Wiping off heavy contamination and preventing blood from drying makes subsequent cleaning much more effective. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why is thorough drying of instruments mandated before they undergo sterilization or chemical disinfection?

options.A: Moisture completely blocks the entry of air into the device
options.B: Wet metal surfaces attract airborne fungal spores rapidly
options.C: Water residue can dilute chemical agents and cause instrument corrosion
options.D: Water increases the electrical conductivity of the packaging

explanation: Residual moisture dilutes liquid disinfectants and promotes rust on metal surfaces during heat sterilization. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h4)

question: Why must chlorine-based disinfectant solutions be prepared fresh on a daily basis?

options.A: Fresh mixtures are required by hospital policy to change color
options.B: Microbes develop immediate resistance to older chlorine mixtures
options.C: Chlorine gas evaporates and the solution loses potency over time
options.D: Old chlorine solutions turn into dangerous acids that dissolve plastic buckets

explanation: Active chlorine dissipates quickly when exposed to air and light, making aged solutions unreliable for disinfection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which factor most significantly reduces the effectiveness of alcohol-based disinfectants on skin or surfaces?

options.A: Exposure to bright fluorescent overhead hospital lighting
options.B: Dilution with sterile normal saline instead of distilled water
options.C: Presence of visible organic matter like blood or dirt
options.D: Application using non-woven gauze instead of cotton balls

explanation: Organic material inactivates alcohol and blocks direct contact with microorganisms, underscoring the need for prior cleaning. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h5)

question: What type of gloves should a nurse wear when manually washing contaminated surgical instruments?

options.A: Heavy-duty utility gloves
options.B: Powder-free examination gloves
options.C: Disposable household latex gloves
options.D: Thin sterile surgical gloves

explanation: Heavy-duty utility gloves provide necessary puncture and chemical resistance during aggressive instrument scrubbing. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended safety feature in a dedicated instrument decontamination room?

options.A: Proper mechanical ventilation and exhaust systems
options.B: Open food and beverage storage refrigerators
options.C: Readily accessible emergency eye-wash stations
options.D: Clearly marked personal protective equipment stations

explanation: Consuming food or storing consumables in a decontamination area creates severe biological contamination risks. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h6)

question: In standard hospital waste management, which color container is typically designated for sharp objects like needles?

options.A: Puncture-proof safety box
options.B: Black municipal bin
options.C: Clear transparent bag
options.D: Blue recycling container

explanation: Sharps must be discarded into rigid, puncture-resistant containers to prevent accidental needle-stick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: A patient's blood spills onto the tiled floor of a ward. What is the correct initial action the nurse should take before applying disinfectant?

options.A: Leave the wet spill uncovered to air-dry completely overnight
options.B: Sweep the liquid across the floor into the nearest drainage outlet
options.C: Flood the entire room with water using a high-pressure hose
options.D: Confine the spill and absorb it with disposable paper towels

explanation: Spills must first be absorbed and cleaned of organic matter before chemical disinfection can be effective. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h7)

question: What is the primary objective of the Central Sterilizing Supply Department?

options.A: Managing hospital linen and patient apparel laundry
options.B: Ensuring reusable medical devices are free of micro-organisms
options.C: Disposing of hazardous chemical waste safely
options.D: Conducting routine maintenance on surgical theatre lights

explanation: The core function of the CSSD is to sterilize and prepare medical equipment to prevent healthcare-associated infections. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: Why is the physical location of the CSSD strategically significant in a hospital?

options.A: It allows patients easy access to pick up surgical instruments for home use
options.B: It minimizes the risk of cross-contamination by separating clean and dirty workflows
options.C: It ensures administrative staff can monitor clinical nursing shifts directly
options.D: It places the department close to the hospital kitchen for easy supply sharing

explanation: Strategic layout and zoning keep soiled instruments away from sterile packaging areas, protecting patients from infectious agents. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which air pressure design is maintained in the decontamination zone of a CSSD?

options.A: Negative air pressure
options.B: Positive air pressure
options.C: Neutral atmospheric pressure
options.D: Variable fluctuating pressure

explanation: Negative pressure stops contaminated air from drifting out of the dirty wash area into clean assembly rooms. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: A student nurse observes instrument trays being wrapped in a clean, positive pressure zone. What is the operational purpose of this design?

options.A: It increases the humidity to prevent delicate rubber tubing from cracking
options.B: It removes toxic chemical fumes produced by the autoclave machines
options.C: It forces air outward to prevent dust and microbes from entering sterile packages
options.D: It cools down hot surgical instruments faster after the washing cycle

explanation: Positive pressure ensures airflow moves from clean areas toward less clean areas, keeping airborne contaminants away from exposed sterile items. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h2)

question: What physical phenomenon does an ultrasonic cleaner rely on to remove debris from narrow instrument crevices?

options.A: Cavitation
options.B: Centrifugation
options.C: Pasteurization
options.D: Evaporation

explanation: Ultrasonic waves create microscopic vacuum bubbles that collapse violently, lifting microscopic soil out of hard-to-reach box locks and hinges. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: Why must surgical instruments undergo thorough manual or mechanical cleaning before entering an autoclave?

options.A: Unwashed metal surfaces expand unevenly and jam the inner chamber door
options.B: Residual tissue proteins react with steam to produce toxic poisonous gases
options.C: Dried organic matter and blood shield micro-organisms, rendering sterilization ineffective
options.D: Dirty instruments will cause the autoclave machine to rust during the drying phase

explanation: Heat and steam cannot destroy pathogens protected underneath layers of dried blood, pus, or tissue protein. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is placed inside every instrument tray before wrapping to verify that sterilizing agents have penetrated the pack?

options.A: A biological spore strip
options.B: A stainless steel identification tag
options.C: A moisture-absorbent silica gel
options.D: A chemical indicator

explanation: Internal chemical indicators react to parameters like heat or steam, showing that the sterilizing medium successfully reached the inside of the pack. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: A nurse inspector finds a surgical hemostat with a misaligned box lock during the assembly phase. What is the correct action to take?

options.A: Proceed with sterilization since high heat will correct the metal alignment
options.B: Send the instrument for repair or replacement before packaging
options.C: Soak the hemostat in enzymatic detergent and immediately autoclave it
options.D: Wrap it tightly in a double layer of linen to secure the jaws

explanation: Faulty instruments compromise surgical efficiency and patient safety, so they must be removed from circulation and repaired or discarded. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h4)

question: What is the primary sterilizing agent used in standard hospital autoclaves?

options.A: Dry radiant electric heat
options.B: Saturated steam under pressure
options.C: Vaporized hydrogen peroxide
options.D: Ethylene oxide chemical gas

explanation: Autoclaves use moist heat in the form of pressurized steam, which denatures microbial proteins rapidly and efficiently. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: A surgical ward sends heat-sensitive plastic tubing and delicate fiber-optic light cables to the CSSD. Which sterilization method is most appropriate?

options.A: Low-temperature gas or vapor sterilization
options.B: High-pressure gravity steam displacement
options.C: High-temperature dry heat convection
options.D: Boiling water immersion for thirty minutes

explanation: Plastics and delicate optics melt or degrade under standard autoclave steam temperatures, requiring low-temperature alternatives like EtO or hydrogen peroxide gas plasma. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: Which bacterial spore is used in biological indicators to test the efficacy of steam sterilization cycles?

options.A: Staphylococcus aureus
options.B: Clostridium tetani
options.C: Geobacillus stearothermophilus
options.D: Bacillus atrophaeus

explanation: Geobacillus stearothermophilus spores are highly resistant to heat, making them the standard biological test organism for validating steam autoclaves. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: Why are biological indicators considered superior to routine mechanical and chemical monitors?

options.A: They change color immediately upon reaching the target holding temperature
options.B: They can be read instantly through the glass door without opening the machine
options.C: They measure exact chamber pressure fluctuations throughout the air removal phase
options.D: They directly test whether actual bacterial spores were destroyed by the cycle

explanation: Biological indicators provide direct proof of microbial lethality rather than just measuring environmental parameters like temperature and time. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h6)

question: What inventory management rule is applied in the CSSD sterile storage area to prevent supplies from expiring or degrading?

options.A: Last-In, First-Out (LIFO)
options.B: First-In, First-Out (FIFO)
options.C: Just-In-Time (JIT) stock purging
options.D: Randomized batch rotation

explanation: The FIFO principle ensures older sterile stock is dispensed first, minimizing waste and preventing prolonged storage wear. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: A nurse in the sterile storage room notices a wrapped instrument tray lying flat on the floor underneath the bottom shelf. What is the appropriate nursing action?

options.A: Treat the pack as contaminated and return it to the CSSD for re-sterilization
options.B: Record the batch number in the ward log and issue it to the operating theatre
options.C: Wipe the outer wrapper with an alcohol swab and place it on the top shelf
options.D: Open the pack immediately to inspect the instruments for floor dust damage

explanation: Items stored on the floor violate basic sterile storage guidelines and are considered contaminated due to proximity to foot traffic and dust. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h7)

question: Which specific protective gear is most essential for staff working in the CSSD decontamination wash area?

options.A: Lead-lined aprons and radiation dosimetry badges
options.B: Waterproof aprons and heavy utility gloves
options.C: Sterile surgical gowns and powder-free gloves
options.D: Disposable paper caps and fabric shoe covers

explanation: Decontamination workers handle gross body fluids and caustic detergents, requiring fluid-resistant garments and puncture-resistant utility gloves. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard occupational safety measure in a hospital CSSD?

options.A: Providing Hepatitis B vaccination for all department personnel
options.B: Allowing staff to eat and drink near the packaging tables during quiet shifts
options.C: Installing emergency eyewash stations near chemical washing sinks
options.D: Using vapor extraction hoods around low-temperature gas sterilizers

explanation: Eating, drinking, and storing food in contaminated or clean processing areas violate universal biosafety standards and are strictly prohibited. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h8)

question: What is the primary function of the Theatre Sterile Supply Unit in a hospital?

options.A: Processing, sterilizing, and distributing surgical instruments
options.B: Manufacturing single-use disposable syringes and gloves
options.C: Performing routine maintenance on operating theatre lights
options.D: Disposing of hazardous medical waste generated in wards

explanation: The core mandate of the TSSU is to ensure that all surgical instruments and medical devices are thoroughly decontaminated, sterilized, and safely delivered back to clinical areas. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why is a unidirectional workflow maintained in a sterile supply unit?

options.A: To speed up the physical packaging of delicate instruments
options.B: To ensure autoclaves operate at maximum electrical capacity
options.C: To reduce the total number of staff required on duty
options.D: To prevent cross-contamination between dirty and clean items

explanation: Moving items strictly forward from soiled reception zones to clean processing and finally to sterile storage stops micro-organisms from recontaminating processed equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: Which zone of the TSSU operates under negative air pressure?

options.A: Decontamination area
options.B: Sterile storage area
options.C: Packaging and assembly room
options.D: Administrative office

explanation: Negative air pressure in the wash area ensures that air flows inward when doors are opened, preventing contaminated aerosols from drifting into clean zones. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the main purpose of positive air pressure in the sterile storage zone?

options.A: To push air outward and prevent dust or microbes from entering
options.B: To cool down newly sterilized metal instruments rapidly
options.C: To eliminate the need for routine environmental surface cleaning
options.D: To accelerate the drying time of packaged linen packs

explanation: Positive pressure forces air out of the room whenever doors open, creating an invisible barrier that protects sterile supplies from airborne contaminants. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h2)

question: What is the primary reason organic debris must be removed before sterilization?

options.A: It protects hidden microorganisms from the sterilizing agent
options.B: It makes the instruments too heavy for safe transport
options.C: It causes metal instruments to change color permanently
options.D: It clogs the plumbing system of mechanical washer-disinfectors

explanation: Residual blood, pus, or tissue acts as a physical barrier that can shield bacteria and spores from steam or chemical sterilants, causing sterilization failure. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: Why should manual cleaning of bloody instruments be performed underwater?

options.A: To cool the cleaning brushes and extend their lifespan
options.B: To prevent the generation of infectious aerosols
options.C: To soften the metal before scrubbing takes place
options.D: To dissolve chemical detergents faster than open air

explanation: Submerging items during scrubbing stops fine droplets containing bloodborne pathogens from spraying into the air and being inhaled by staff. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h3)

question: Which device is commonly used during the inspection phase to detect small flaws on instruments?

options.A: Pressure manometer
options.B: Digital thermometer
options.C: Ultraviolet scanner
options.D: Magnifying lamp

explanation: Magnifying lamps provide enhanced visibility, enabling staff to spot microscopic cracks, rust, or residual organic debris on delicate surgical tips. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: What essential characteristic must packaging material possess for successful sterilization?

options.A: High electrical conductivity to dissipate static electricity during storage
options.B: Absolute impermeability to air, moisture, and all gases at all times
options.C: Complete transparency so contents can be counted without opening
options.D: Permeability to the sterilizing agent and subsequent barrier protection

explanation: The wrap must let steam or gas reach the inside during the cycle, yet block microbes from entering once the pack is removed from the sterilizer. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h4)

question: Which organism is used as the biological indicator for steam sterilization cycles?

options.A: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.B: Escherichia coli
options.C: Geobacillus stearothermophilus
options.D: Staphylococcus aureus

explanation: Spores of this heat-resistant bacterium are standard test organisms used to verify that an autoclave has achieved conditions capable of destroying tough microbial life. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is the main limitation of chemical indicator strips placed on instrument packs?

options.A: They expire within 24 hours of being exposed to room temperature air
options.B: They can only be read accurately under ultraviolet lighting conditions
options.C: They show exposure to parameters like heat or gas, but do not prove sterility
options.D: They must be sent to an external laboratory for microscopic evaluation

explanation: A color change on a chemical indicator confirms that the pack experienced certain conditions such as heat, but it does not guarantee that biological spores were completely killed. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: What inventory principle ensures older sterile stock is used before newly processed items?

options.A: Maximum Stock Level
options.B: First-In, First-Out (FIFO)
options.C: Just-In-Time (JIT) supply
options.D: Batch Processing Control

explanation: Applying FIFO stock rotation prevents supplies from lingering in storage indefinitely, reducing waste and the risk of expired sterile barriers. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: Why must freshly autoclaved packs be allowed to cool completely before being handled?

options.A: Hot packaging materials are chemically unstable and release toxic vapors
options.B: Rapid cooling is required to set the chemical indicator color permanently
options.C: Warm packs can absorb moisture from the hands and environment, contaminating the contents
options.D: Handling hot metal trays causes immediate damage to internal instrument hinges

explanation: Condensation forms easily on warm paper or woven wraps; moisture acts as a wick that pulls bacteria right through the wrapper into the sterile zone inside. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h6)

question: Which personal protective equipment is essential for staff working in the TSSU decontamination area?

options.A: High-filtration particulate respirator without eye protection
options.B: Sterile surgical gown and sterile powder-free latex gloves
options.C: Waterproof apron, face shield, and heavy utility gloves
options.D: Disposable paper lab coat and non-slip canvas shoes

explanation: The wash area exposes workers to chemical splashes, hot water, and bloodborne pathogens, requiring barrier protection for the eyes, face, torso, and hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended infection control practice in a TSSU?

options.A: Eating meals at the sorting workbench during quiet shift hours
options.B: Maintaining negative air pressure in the instrument decontamination room
options.C: Wearing heavy-duty utility gloves while operating the manual wash sink
options.D: Performing regular biological spore testing on all autoclave equipment

explanation: Consuming food or beverages in areas where contaminated instruments are handled creates a severe route of ingestion for biological pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of respiratory protection in healthcare settings?

options.A: Filtering dust particles from hospital construction zones
options.B: Keeping the healthcare worker's face warm in air-conditioned wards
options.C: Preventing the inhalation of infectious aerosols and droplets
options.D: Masking unpleasant hospital odors during wound dressings

explanation: Respiratory protection acts as a physical barrier to block infectious agents transmitted through the air or respiratory droplets. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h1)

question: Why must nurses evaluate the transmission route of a pathogen before entering a patient's room?

options.A: To decide whether the patient needs immediate surgical intervention
options.B: To calculate the exact dosage of prophylactic antibiotics required
options.C: To determine how long the hospital room window should remain open
options.D: To choose the correct type of personal protective equipment barrier

explanation: Different pathogens require specific barriers, such as surgical masks for droplets versus particulate respirators for airborne nuclei. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h1)

question: What is the primary function of a standard surgical mask?

options.A: Providing an airtight seal around the entire nose and chin
options.B: Containing respiratory emissions and large droplets from the wearer
options.C: Supplying supplemental oxygen during emergency resuscitation
options.D: Filtering out microscopic airborne viral particles completely

explanation: Surgical masks are primarily designed as source control to catch droplets expelled by the person wearing them. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h2)

question: Which surgical mask rating provides the highest level of fluid resistance against blood splashes?

options.A: Level 1 or Type I
options.B: Standard paper barrier
options.C: Basic cloth face covering
options.D: Level 3 or Type IIR

explanation: Level 3 and Type IIR masks are specifically engineered to withstand high-velocity splashes of blood and bodily fluids. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h2)

question: What percentage of very small test particles must an N95 respirator filter out to meet its standard?

options.A: 100 percent without exception
options.B: Exactly 50 percent
options.C: At least 95 percent
options.D: Up to 80 percent maximum

explanation: The designation N95 indicates that the filter captures a minimum of 95 percent of specified test particles. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h3)

question: Why is achieving a tight facial seal critical when wearing an N95 respirator?

options.A: It prevents unfiltered air from leaking around the edges of the device
options.B: It allows the mask to be reused across multiple shifts safely
options.C: It stops the wearer from touching their face with unwashed hands
options.D: It ensures the mask stays firmly attached during physical exercise

explanation: If a seal is broken, air takes the path of least resistance and bypasses the filter material entirely. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h3)

question: When is a particulate respirator like an N95 specifically indicated over a surgical mask?

options.A: When caring for patients with airborne-spread infections like tuberculosis
options.B: When handing out food trays in a general medical ward
options.C: When visiting a patient with a clean surgical wound
options.D: When performing routine bed bath procedures on stable patients

explanation: Airborne pathogens require high-efficiency particulate respirators because they remain suspended in air and travel further. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h4)

question: A nurse is preparing to enter an isolation room for a patient newly admitted with suspected pulmonary tuberculosis. Which protective device must the nurse select?

options.A: A standard loose-fitting paper surgical mask
options.B: A sterile operating theatre face shield only
options.C: A reusable fabric face covering with ties
options.D: An N95 or higher particulate respirator

explanation: Pulmonary tuberculosis is transmitted via airborne nuclei, necessitating a fitted particulate respirator rather than a surgical mask. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h4)

question: What is the purpose of performing a user seal check after donning an N95 respirator?

options.A: To test the battery level of the mechanical filtration motor
options.B: To confirm that air does not leak around the edges of the mask
options.C: To check if the elastic straps can be adjusted to fit a colleague
options.D: To ensure the inner lining is completely dry from perspiration

explanation: A user seal check ensures proper fit and confirms that air passes through the filter media rather than gaps. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h5)

question: Why is annual fit testing required for healthcare workers who wear tight-fitting respirators?

options.A: Hospital regulations require retraining staff on basic hand hygiene yearly
options.B: Respiratory filters expire chemically after exactly twelve months
options.C: Manufacturers change the color of the straps every year
options.D: Facial structure changes such as weight fluctuations can alter the mask seal

explanation: Changes in facial weight, dental work, or scarring can break a previously adequate seal, necessitating re-evaluation. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which part of a used mask is considered contaminated and should NEVER be touched during removal?

options.A: The side edges near the ears
options.B: The elastic head straps
options.C: The front exterior filtering surface
options.D: The bottom fastening band

explanation: The front surface accumulates pathogens during use, so handling it directly transfers contaminants to the hands. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h6)

question: When removing a dual-strap respirator, why should the bottom strap be unfastened and lifted over the head before the top strap?

options.A: It satisfies standard hospital administrative paperwork requirements
options.B: It locks the metal nosepiece in place for easier cleaning later
options.C: It prevents the mask from swinging forward and contaminating the face or chest
options.D: It makes the elastic bands easier to stretch for the next person's use

explanation: Releasing the bottom strap first allows the mask to drop safely away from the breathing zone without flipping onto the wearer. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h6)

question: Which of the following practices is an infection control violation when wearing a medical mask?

options.A: Disposing of the mask immediately in a biohazard container
options.B: Performing hand hygiene before touching the elastic straps
options.C: Checking the nose clip contour for a secure fit
options.D: Pulling the mask down under the chin while talking or resting

explanation: Pulling a mask under the chin exposes the nose and mouth and contaminates the inner lining with neck bacteria. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h7)

question: Why must a surgical mask or respirator be replaced immediately if it becomes damp or wet?

options.A: Moisture destroys the filtration efficiency and facilitates microbial strike-through
options.B: Wet elastic bands lose their stretch and make the mask fall off
options.C: Damp masks change color and violate hospital dress code policies
options.D: Water droplets chemically dissolve the plastic materials instantly

explanation: Moisture compromises the barrier properties of filter media, allowing microorganisms to pass through easily. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T9#GNS122_U2_T9_h7)

question: What is the primary goal of injection safety in clinical practice?

options.A: Minimizing the physical pain experienced by the patient
options.B: Ensuring procedures do no harm to recipients, providers, and communities
options.C: Accelerating the speed at which medications are absorbed
options.D: Reducing the overall cost of purchasing disposable syringes

explanation: Injection safety focuses holistically on protecting patients, health workers, and the public from preventable biological hazards. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why is rigorous training in injection safety particularly critical for student nurses?

options.A: It is the only way to pass mandatory licensing board examinations without remediation
options.B: It establishes a lifelong standard of safe, accountable clinical habits early in their career
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never experience localized bruising or swelling
options.D: It eliminates the need to wear sterile gloves during subcutaneous drug delivery

explanation: Building proper muscle memory and adherence to safety protocols during training prevents dangerous shortcuts in later practice. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h1)

question: The scope of injection safety concludes with which of the following actions?

options.A: Obtaining verbal consent before the procedure begins
options.B: Documenting the drug batch number in the patient chart
options.C: Applying a dry cotton swab over the puncture site
options.D: Immediate, secure containment of the used sharp device

explanation: The safety cycle finishes only when sharps are safely deposited into a puncture-resistant container to prevent secondary injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: What happens to an injection procedure if a single step in the safety chain fails?

options.A: It remains safe as long as the medication itself is sterile
options.B: The patient is protected provided they have received past vaccinations
options.C: Only the healthcare provider faces a risk of blood exposure
options.D: The entire procedure is classified as unsafe and hazardous

explanation: Injection safety relies on an unbroken chain of precautions; a failure anywhere compromises the integrity of the whole process. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h2)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what defines a safe injection?

options.A: A technique that utilizes glass ampoules rather than plastic multi-dose vials
options.B: An injection that harms no one, exposes providers to no avoidable risk, and creates safe waste
options.C: A subcutaneous procedure performed exclusively by registered nurses
options.D: An intervention costing less than standard oral medication therapies

explanation: The WHO definition emphasizes three pillars: protection of the patient, protection of the healthcare worker, and safe waste management. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: Why do regulatory health frameworks strictly discourage the manual recapping of used needles?

options.A: It alters the chemical composition of the remaining medication in the barrel
options.B: It prevents the proper sterilization of reusable stainless steel syringes
options.C: It is the leading mechanical cause of accidental occupational needle-stick injuries
options.D: It delays the administration time during emergency resuscitation scenarios

explanation: Attempting to guide a needle back into its cap frequently results in the hand slipping and puncturing the skin, transmitting pathogens. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following bloodborne viruses poses the highest risk of transmission through a single needle-stick injury?

options.A: Human Immunodeficiency Virus
options.B: Hepatitis B virus
options.C: Epstein-Barr virus
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Hepatitis B has a significantly higher concentration in blood and viral stability, making it the most easily transmitted pathogen via sharps injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: A patient develops a warm, fluctuant, and extremely painful swelling at the site of a previous intramuscular injection given a week ago. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Accidental puncture of a deep subcutaneous nerve branch
options.B: Introduction of bacteria due to a breach in aseptic technique
options.C: Rapid absorption of the drug into the surrounding adipose tissue
options.D: A normal localized hypersensitivity reaction to the preservative

explanation: A localized collection of pus or abscess formation typically indicates bacterial contamination introduced during the injection process. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the correct method for applying an alcohol swab to skin prior to an injection?

options.A: From the outer perimeter directly toward the center of the site
options.B: In a circular motion starting from the center and moving outward
options.C: Vertically up and down along the expected path of the needle
options.D: In a rigorous back-and-forth scrubbing motion across the muscle fibers

explanation: Starting at the center and moving outward sweeps mechanical contaminants away from the clean puncture zone. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why is it unacceptable to use the same syringe for multiple patients if you change the needle between them?

options.A: Syringes lose their vacuum seal and cannot draw accurate medication dosages
options.B: The syringe barrel and plunger can become contaminated with blood or fluids during use
options.C: New needles are manufactured with different threading that does not fit old barrels
options.D: Regulatory laws permit multi-patient syringes only in surgical operating theatres

explanation: Backflow into the barrel during aspiration or injection contaminates the internal components, making the syringe unsafe for another person regardless of a needle change. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h5)

question: At what capacity should a sharps disposal container be permanently sealed and replaced?

options.A: Three-quarters full
options.B: At the end of every individual nursing shift
options.C: Completely packed to the absolute brim
options.D: One-quarter full to ensure lightweight handling

explanation: Sealing containers at three-quarters capacity prevents protruding needles and accidental punctures from overfilled openings. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary operational hazard of placing a sharps container far away from where injections are administered?

options.A: It causes the sterile medication inside the syringe to degrade from light exposure
options.B: It violates international medication dosage calculation formulas
options.C: It prevents accurate documentation of the injection time in the patient record
options.D: It forces staff to walk with exposed needles, drastically increasing the risk of a needle-stick injury

explanation: Sharps containers must be kept immediately accessible to prevent hazardous transit of uncapped needles across clinical spaces. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T1#GNS122_U3_T1_h6)

question: Which bloodborne pathogen is most efficiently transmitted through contaminated medical injections?

options.A: Hepatitis C virus
options.B: Mycobacterium tuberculosis
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Plasmodium falciparum

explanation: Parenteral exposure via contaminated needles carries a very high transmission efficiency for bloodborne viruses, particularly hepatitis C, hepatitis B, and HIV. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: What is the primary operational hazard of reusing a disposable plastic syringe in clinical practice?

options.A: Immediate crystallization of injected medication
options.B: Cross-contamination with residual pathogens
options.C: Microscopic dulling of the needle bevel
options.D: Rapid degradation of the plastic barrel

explanation: Pathogens left inside the dead space of a syringe or needle can directly enter the bloodstream of the next patient, causing systemic infection. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h1)

question: According to the World Health Organization, what defines a safe injection?

options.A: An injection that utilizes a retractable needle and a safety-engineered winged set
options.B: One that causes no harm to the recipient, poses no risk to the provider, and creates no hazardous waste
options.C: Any parenteral medication delivery performed inside a sterile operating theater
options.D: One that is administered exclusively by a registered physician using a glass syringe

explanation: The WHO comprehensive definition explicitly encompasses the safety of the patient, the healthcare worker, and the surrounding community. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is the first operational step a nurse should take to align with WHO core injection safety principles?

options.A: Soak all used metal needles in a strong chlorine solution before disposal
options.B: Assess whether an oral alternative to the prescribed medication is clinically effective
options.C: Recap every syringe immediately after administration to protect colleagues
options.D: Store used safety boxes in the patient ward until the end of the shift

explanation: Reducing unnecessary injections by selecting oral routes whenever possible is a core preventative tenet of global injection safety guidelines. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h2)

question: What is recognized as the single most effective intervention to prevent healthcare-associated infections during clinical procedures?

options.A: Routine administration of prophylactic antibiotics
options.B: Rigorous hand hygiene compliance
options.C: Wearing heavy utility gloves at all times
options.D: Ultraviolet disinfection of treatment rooms

explanation: Hand hygiene interrupts the transmission of pathogens carried on the hands of healthcare workers between patients and sterile equipment. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: When must a nurse perform hand hygiene in relation to preparing an aseptic injection?

options.A: Only when the patient has a known infectious disease diagnosis
options.B: Before entering the hospital ward at the start of the morning shift
options.C: After disposing of the used syringe into the safety box
options.D: Immediately before preparing the medication and after the procedure is finished

explanation: Aseptic technique requires hand hygiene immediately prior to touching sterile supplies to avoid introducing environmental microbes into the medication pathway. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h3)

question: What is the primary mechanical feature of an Auto-Disable (AD) syringe?

options.A: It automatically jams or breaks after a single injection to prevent reuse
options.B: It measures exact dosages without requiring manual plunger alignment
options.C: It neutralizes bloodborne viruses using an internal chemical coating
options.D: It features a built-in metal shield that covers the needle tip upon impact

explanation: Auto-disable technology is engineered to render the syringe permanently inoperable after one complete stroke, eliminating accidental or intentional reuse. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h4)

question: Why is pre-filling multiple syringes prior to a mass immunization clinic strongly discouraged?

options.A: It compromises sterility and creates high risks of bacterial growth and medication errors
options.B: It causes the plastic barrel to dissolve when exposed to ambient room lighting
options.C: It increases the total weight of the medication tray beyond safe carrying limits
options.D: It forces the plunger mechanism to lock before the nurse reaches the patient

explanation: Drawn medications left sitting in syringes lose sterility and run a high risk of microbial proliferation or being administered to the wrong recipient. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h4)

question: What is the maximum recommended fill level for a sharps disposal container before it must be permanently sealed?

options.A: Three-quarters full
options.B: Half full
options.C: Completely filled to the brim
options.D: One-quarter full

explanation: Stopping at the three-quarters mark prevents accidental punctures that occur when pushing items into an overly packed container. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: Which of the following actions is NOT permitted when handling used injection equipment?

options.A: Discarding the syringe and needle as a single unit without separation
options.B: Recapping the needle with two hands immediately after an injection
options.C: Inspecting the container to ensure it rests on a stable surface
options.D: Placing the puncture-resistant safety box close to the point of use

explanation: Manual recapping is a primary cause of needle-stick injuries and is strictly prohibited by international safety standards. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h5)

question: What is the immediate first-aid action a nurse should take after sustaining an accidental needle-stick injury?

options.A: Apply a concentrated iodine tincture and cover with airtight tape
options.B: Soak the affected finger in a basin of domestic bleach solution
options.C: Squeeze the wound vigorously to force out all trapped venous blood
options.D: Wash the puncture site thoroughly with soap and clean running water

explanation: Immediate washing with soap and water removes surface contaminants, while harsh scrubbing or caustic chemicals should be avoided to prevent mucosal damage. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)

question: When does the highest risk of sustaining a needle-stick injury typically occur during a clinical procedure?

options.A: While opening the sterile paper packaging of a brand-new syringe
options.B: While administering oral medications to an uncooperative patient
options.C: When sliding an unpunctured safety box into a transport carton
options.D: During or immediately after attempting to recap a used needle

explanation: Attempts to guide a contaminated needle back into its small cap frequently result in missed entries and finger punctures. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h6)

question: What is a primary logistical barrier to maintaining injection safety in resource-limited clinical settings?

options.A: Interrupted supply chains for auto-disable syringes and safety boxes
options.B: Lack of patient willingness to receive any form of intramuscular therapy
options.C: Excessive availability of sterile glass syringes and autoclaves
options.D: Overabundance of professional nursing personnel in rural clinics

explanation: Stockouts of safety-engineered devices and disposal containers often force clinicians into improvised, hazardous practices. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h7)

question: How can a nurse leader effectively monitor and improve injection safety compliance on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Require patients to purchase and bring their own disposable needles
options.B: Conduct supportive supervision and ensure continuous availability of safety boxes
options.C: Punish junior staff publicly whenever an injection error is reported
options.D: Prohibit the administration of all parenteral medications across the facility

explanation: Supportive supervision combined with reliable supplies creates an enabling environment where safety protocols can be consistently followed. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T10#GNS122_U3_T10_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of monitoring injection safety devices in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To calculate monthly staff salaries for the pharmacy department
options.B: To prevent infection transmission and occupational injuries
options.C: To determine the total electricity consumption of the clinic
options.D: To evaluate the culinary hygiene of the hospital cafeteria

explanation: Routine surveillance of injection devices ensures safe administration practices, directly minimizing the risk of bloodborne pathogen spread and needlestick injuries. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: Why is monthly monitoring particularly crucial in resource-constrained healthcare environments?

options.A: It guarantees that patients never experience pain during injections
options.B: It prevents supply chain gaps and the use of substandard materials
options.C: It automatically generates international funding for the facility
options.D: It replaces the need for any clinical supervision or training

explanation: Regular checks help catch missing supplies, expired stock, or broken safety equipment before they compromise patient and staff safety. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T11#GNS122_U3_T11_h1)

question: What metric is typically evaluated by comparing safety boxes used to total injection devices expended?

options.A: Patient satisfaction rates
options.B: Waste management tracking
options.C: Building maintenance costs
